WHAT YOU'LL BRING: - Proven Experience: Extensive experience in UI/UX design, with background leading design projects from ideation to launch. - Curiosity: Passion for deeply understanding user needs and finding the right solutions from first principles. - Full-Stack Design: Visual design is the baseline. You should be fluent in creating beautiful, high-quality designs—working end-to-end from shaping product direction to defining the right interactions and ensuring every pixel is crafted with care. - Great Collaboration: Design is a team sport, and building great products means working closely with product, engineering, and leadership to help bring ideas to life. - Excellent Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate problems, design concepts and decisions to various stakeholders. - Research Skills: Experience gathering customer feedback, usability testing, and translating findings into actionable design improvements. - Technical Proficiency: Fluent in Figma and comfortable picking up new tools quickly, especially AI tools. EVEN BETTER... - Experience designing for AI-driven products or conversational interfaces. - Experience working on developer-driven products, including SDKs, APIs, and technical tooling. OUR VALUES - Trust: We do the right thing, even when no one is looking, and even when it’s hard. When we screw up, we take accountability, fully and completely. We do whatever it takes to make our customers successful, and we go the extra mile in how we show up as a partner with unreasonable hospitality. - Craftsmanship: A great company is the aggregation of thousands of things done well. As they say, “how you do anything is how you do everything”. Most important is craftsmanship in building agents that are so great that people thank them at the end of a call. That’s the standard. - Intensity: We operate with urgency, and we want to win. We are never complacent. We fight to win every deal, big or small, using the full force of the company. And when we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time. - Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. The raise follows a breakout year, with our business growing 8x as enterprise customers across industries adopt our category, AI‑moderated research, as the new standard for understanding people. We’re a tight-knit team serving some of the world’s largest enterprises. We're looking for an experienced product designer to join our small team and own meaningful parts of the Outset product. jobs.title: Product Designer, Accessibility
jobs.descriptionText: About the Team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Design Systems team creates the foundations that help teams across OpenAI build coherent, high-quality experiences at scale. Accessibility is fundamental to that work. We’re building the shared standards, components, tools, and practices that make inclusive experiences the default across OpenAI’s products and platforms. About the Role In this role, you’ll lead OpenAI’s company-wide accessibility program from within the Design Foundations team within Product Design. You’ll pair strategy and organizational influence with hands-on product design (visual and interaction design) —advocating for disabled people, removing barriers across complete customer journeys, and establishing durable ownership throughout the company. This is an opportunity to define accessibility for a new generation of products spanning web, mobile, desktop, voice, AI, and hardware. You’ll help teams consider the many ways people perceive, understand, navigate, and interact with technology, going beyond minimum compliance to create experiences that are genuinely useful and inclusive. Working across design, engineering, research, product, go-to-market, and legal, you’ll make accessibility an expected part of product quality—not a final review or the responsibility of a single expert. This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role you will: - Design and ship product experiences while identifying systemic barriers across complete customer journeys. - Define OpenAI’s accessibility strategy, roadmap, governance, priorities, and measures of progress. - Build accessibility into our design system through inclusive components, tokens, interaction patterns, Figma libraries, documentation, and engineering guardrails. - Center disabled people through participatory research, usability studies, and assistive-technology testing rather than relying solely on assumptions, simulations, or automated tools. - Design for permanent, temporary, and situational disabilities, including multiple ways to perceive information, navigate interfaces, understand content, and complete important tasks. - Establish practical standards for screen readers, keyboard navigation, focus, reading order, contrast, typography, motion, captions, forms, errors, and multimodal interactions. - Lead accessibility audits, remediation priorities, launch readiness, and continuous validation across platforms. - Partner with go-to-market, legal, compliance, and product teams on enterprise readiness, accessibility documentation, procurement needs, and customer commitments. - Grow company-wide capability through training, critiques, engineering partnerships, and a network of accessibility champions. You might thrive in this role if you: - Pair deep accessibility expertise with a very high bar for design craft: strong interaction design, visual design, systems thinking, and prototyping skills - Have led accessibility or inclusive-design work across multiple teams, products, or platforms. - Understand the relationship between accessibility, usability, and inclusive design—and know when to go beyond standards to meet real human needs. - Have deep practical knowledge of WCAG, assistive technologies, accessible interaction design, and platform-specific standards. - Have embedded accessibility into design systems, reusable components, and engineering workflows. - Have worked directly with disabled people and translated their experiences into meaningful product and organizational decisions. - Can identify assumptions and exclusion within a product journey, then turn those insights into clearer and more flexible ways to interact. - Are equally effective setting strategy, designing detailed experiences, and collaborating with engineers through implementation. - Can influence across disciplines without direct authority, creating shared accountability without becoming a centralized approval gate. With $43M in funding from Founders Fund, Greylock, Hanabi, and Dylan Field who led our Series B, we helped our customers book hundreds of thousands of jobs across services industries in North America. There are now companies operating entirely AI-first on Netic. You’ll join our team with relentless builders from Scale, Databricks, HRT, Meta, MIT, Stanford, and Harvard in bringing frontier AI to the physical economy, where the problems are hard, the data is complex, and the impact is immediate and tangible. jobs.title: Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT NASH Nash powers logistics infrastructure for major commerce brands including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, and 7-Eleven, plus platforms like Shopify and Toast. We unify decisioning, execution, and capacity into a programmable platform for real-time, AI-native logistics orchestration across couriers, fleets, gig workers, and autonomous systems. Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman and Aziz Alghunaim. We are backed by Y Combinator, a16z, OpenAI, and other leading investors, and headquartered in San Francisco. ABOUT THE ROLE This is not a classic "make it pretty" design role. We're looking for a Product Designer at the intersection of UX and design engineering — someone who deeply understands users and discovers customer needs with ease, but is also technical enough to think in components, speak the language of engineers, and ship a working prototype instead of a static mock when that's the fastest path to an answer. You'll design the tools dispatchers, ops managers, and drivers rely on every day — dense, real-time, operational interfaces — and help define what an agentic-AI-native logistics product feels like. - ~70% web application, ~30% mobile - Optimized for speed: fast progress, rapid iteration, short concept-to-validation loops - Embedded with engineering teams and sales — you design with developers, and partner with sales to gather first-hand customer needs and bring them back into the product - Process mindset: Define → Build → Test → Design → Ship — we validate real, working software early, instead of the classic define → design → build → test → ship (the old double diamond) - Small design team, high ownership, direct access and customers/users. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Discover and validate customer needs — interviews, feedback analysis, synthesis into design decisions - Design dense, operational web UI: dispatch workspaces, routing, agents, order management, real-time views, data visualization - Create concepts and prototypes rapidly — in Figma or in code, using AI tools (Claude, Cursor, v0, Figma Make) as a core part of your workflow - Prepare and run client-facing demos; present, persuade, and defend design decisions with stakeholders - Contribute to and evolve our design system (components, tokens, variables) - Drive the agentic AI approach in the product experience — make AI-first workflows feel native for logistics operators - Work day-to-day inside engineering teams: refine scope, resolve feasibility trade-offs, keep quality high through implementation WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 7+ years of product / UX design experience with shipped work in complex products - Proven B2B product experience — complex workflows, professional users, data-dense interfaces - Strong discovery skills: you get to the real customer problem quickly and can show how research shaped your decisions - Component-based thinking: atomic design, modern web patterns for web applications, understanding of how design maps to frontend implementation - Technical fluency — comfortable working directly with engineers, understanding constraints, reading a design token file - Active, daily use of LLMs and AI prototyping tools as part of your design workflow - Bias for fast iteration: you'd rather ship three rough rounds than one polished big-bang - Clear communication in English; comfortable presenting to clients; adaptable to evidence NICE-TO-HAVES - Design systems depth: tokens, variables, theming, Figma component architecture - Design engineering / prototyping in code: React, Tailwind, or AI tools (v0, Cursor, Claude) - Experience with logistics, supply chain, or ops tooling - Experience designing agentic AI / LLM-powered product experiences - Mobile design experience (iOS / Android patterns) More about Nash http://Nash.AI NASH IS THE PLATFORM THAT POWERS MODERN LOGISTICS. Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line. Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion. We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it. Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco. WHAT YOU’LL LOVE ABOUT US ✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career! ✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates ✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity ✅ Flexible paid time off ✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance for US employees

jobs.title: Product Design
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT US Medical data exchange is one of the biggest unsolved problems in US healthcare. If you've spent any real time in the healthcare system, you've felt it, and it only gets worse the sicker and older you get. Metriport exists to fix that. We connect to the data sources the healthcare providers of tomorrow need, take raw data that's unusable in its source form, and turn it into a single clean format that care teams, and their agents, actually use to improve outcomes. Record retrieval across thousands of legacy systems and antiquated data pipes that used to take weeks now takes seconds. Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it. We're not a healthcare company. We're a technology company that happens to operate in healthcare, and we build every layer ourselves: connect, transform, and insight. Legacy EHRs were built to get providers paid, not to serve the clinical experience. We're building what should have existed instead: the system of record for all of US healthcare. We started in data exchange. Today we compete with the largest data platforms in the space. Tomorrow we will be the infrastructure layer healthcare runs on. We’ve raised $28.4 million from top tier VCs (including Matrix, ARTIS and Y Combinator), found product market fit (multi million dollar ARR, 100+ customers including Amazon One Medical, Circle Medical, Color Health, and Strive Health), and have years of runway ahead of us. If you’ve had a good healthcare experience in the past few years, there’s a good chance Metriport was behind it. That’s the version of healthcare we want people to not just expect, but demand. Join us and build the future. About You We're a small, high output team, mostly former founders including YC alumni, and we operate with real autonomy and almost no bureaucracy. We hire on competence, not pedigree. Leaders are in the office six days a week, and we generally expect the team to be available six days a week too. Not because we count hours, but because there's always more wood to chop when revolutionizing how tomorrow’s healthcare providers deliver care to their patients today. We trust our team to take the time off they need and we've never said no to a time off request. You have an entrepreneurial mindset and a strong sense of ownership. You don't wait to be told what's broken. Instead, you believe you can figure out any problem that lands in your lap even outside your exact domain. When someone scopes something for three weeks, you ask why it can't be done in three days, and you also know the difference between shipping a fast v0 and cutting a corner that comes back to bite you. You walk the tightrope between craft and speed without falling off either side. The Role As a Founding Designer at Metriport, you'll spend your time understanding customer workflows, defining the right solution to those problems, and making sure everything we ship product, marketing, brand, looks and feels right. The upside is real autonomy: you set the design standard, you own the output, and you're not waiting on anyone else's approval. The tradeoff is that the scope is wide and the bar is high. If that sounds like too much, it probably is. If it sounds like exactly enough, keep reading. At Metriport we think of design like a rough hewn yet elegant table: does its job, looks right in the room, built to last, and finished. You'll bring that sensibility to everything, knowing when a decision needs more thought and when it needs to ship. We strongly believe in the 80/20 rule, and rely on everyone joining our team to use it so that we can ship fast and continue to delight our users. What You'll Do Build and maintain the design system Establish a coherent design language components, spacing, typography, color that is simple and that engineers can build to without hand holding. Design features end to end Take features from rough concept to detailed spec, working closely with founders, PM, and engineers to ship solutions that are functional and feel considered. Talk to, and advocate for, users Understand their workflows, form an opinionated view on the right solution, and drive toward it. Own brand and marketing design Design across all marketing surfaces, website, sales collateral, event materials. You're the person we turn to when anything needs to look good. Requirements - Design instincts: You produce Figma work that is considered and defensible with clear opinions on typography, hierarchy, and interaction patterns. - Pragmatism: You know what to polish and what to ship. You walk the tightrope between craft and speed without falling off either side. - Technical literacy: You know enough about how software gets built to write specs engineers can use and have real tradeoff conversations. - The "Metriport" Mindset: Low ego, high ownership. You ask "Why can't this be done in 3 days?" instead of 3 weeks. BENEFITS - Competitive equity + compensation package 🚀 - Full family Platinum health insurance, dental, and vision coverage 🦷 - 401(k) retirement plan + matching 💰 - Flexible work from home or in office 🏢 - Healthy lunches are complimentary when working in office (and breakfast + dinners as needed) 🍏 - MacBook provided by us 💻 - Unlimited PTO (we work hard, but trust you to take time you need to be at your best) 🧘‍♂️ Our tech On the frontend, we use React on the backend, we rely on Node.js and TypeScript for writing core business logic. We deploy a wide range of AWS cloud services (ie ECS, Fargate, Lambda, etc), and manage our infrastructure as code with AWS CDK. Data lives in PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, S3, Snowflake, HAPI FHIR servers, and more. Metriport provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

jobs.title: Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: At Lapel, we believe the most hospitable companies win. We're building the data, infrastructure, and tools that help customer-facing teams understand every customer and act on that insight at scale throughout the entire customer lifecycle. Most internet businesses want to treat customers well, but their tools work against them. We’re building the layer that makes every interaction feel personal again: unifying context, coordinating action, and closing the gap between intent and experience. It’s a technically ambitious challenge spanning data infrastructure, AI, and systems design – with a deeply human outcome: helping software companies serve people better. We call it hospitality at scale. We’re well-funded, backed by top-tier investors, and already working with exceptional companies, from fast-growing startups to large enterprises. We’ll share more details when we talk. ABOUT THIS ROLE This is a design role for someone who thinks in systems and builds with code. You will own the end-to-end design of Lapel's product, from early concepts to polished interfaces, and be expected to bring both taste and technical fluency to everything you ship. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own product design end-to-end, from zero-to-one concepts to shipped interfaces - Build Lapel's design system from scratch: tokens, components, patterns, docs - Sit with founders and engineers daily, moving from sketch to Figma to PR in hours, not weeks - Ship production-ready designs, often pairing directly with engineers in the codebase - Set the craft bar for the company and defend it as we grow YOU'LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have 3+ years of experience owning product design at a software company - Have strong design sensibility across design systems, layouts, and interactions - Think in systems and build components that scale, not one-offs - Are comfortable writing code and actively use AI tools to bring designs to life - Are opinionated about quality, but collaborative in execution - Move fast while maintaining attention to detail and craft THE PROCESS We aim to hire with intention, respect your time, and offer feedback along the way. 1. Initial conversation (20 minutes) We'll explore your motivations, share what we're building, and answer your questions. 2. Take-home project (2–4 hours) You'll complete a short, well-scoped exercise that mirrors the kind of work you'd do here. 3. In-depth interview (60 minutes) We'll go deeper into your craft and experience. No live coding. No prep work necessary. 4. On-site visit (1–2 days) Join us in the office to review your take-home, grab lunch, and work on something real. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS We believe great people build great companies – and we invest accordingly. - Competitive salary + meaningful early-stage equity - Full benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401(k), and commuter benefits - Generous time off: many company holidays and coordinated team-wide breaks throughout the year to focus and recharge - Office perks: lunch and dinner provided daily, in-office snacks, and health & wellness benefits - Team culture: regular off-sites, tight feedback loops, and a bias toward action WHY LAPEL, WHY NOW 1. A trillion-dollar problem hiding in plain sight. Companies spend over $1T a year on customer-facing teams and $150B on the tools meant to support them, yet every team still pieces context together across a dozen disconnected systems. We're rebuilding this from the foundation, and AI makes now the only moment it's possible. 2. The most interesting place to apply AI is where the work actually happens. Customer operations is one of the largest, most under-built surfaces in software. Every company runs on it, every team feels the pain, and the tools haven't been seriously reimagined in fifteen years. We think the next generation of category-defining B2B companies will be built here. 3. One platform, every customer-facing team. Sales, success, support, and ops all serve the same customer relationship, but each one buys a different tool to do it. Owning the foundation means the surface area grows with the company, from a single team to the entire revenue org to the whole business. That's the market, and the mission: better service at internet scale. Lapel works in person in San Francisco, five days a week, at our office on Market Street. We hire people who'd be restless anywhere else. OTHER NOTICES We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. jobs.title: Founding Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: 🏛️ ABOUT GOVWELL We the people — and the taxpayers — deserve good government. Yet today, interacting with government services is often frustrating and inefficient. GovWell is building the AI operating system transforming how governments serve communities, starting with local agencies. GovWell replaces legacy software for municipalities and counties, empowering public servants to radically streamline public services and cut internal processing time for permits and licenses by up to 95%. Founded in 2023, GovWell powers 5,000+ mission-critical processes for agencies in 35+ states serving millions of residents. The company has raised $35M in funding from Insight Partners, Work-Bench, and Bienville Capital, and the team works in person at GovWell HQ in New York City. Read more about our founding story in TechCrunch https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/29/govwell-is-bringing-automation-and-efficiency-to-local-governments/. 🌟 ROLE OVERVIEW Government software has historically forced users to choose between two bad options: outdated systems that are painful to use, or newer tools that look better but can’t handle the complexity of how government actually works. We believe the next generation of government software should do neither. It should make extraordinarily complex workflows feel simple, intuitive, and even delightful. GovWell is hiring a Founding Product Designer to define what that future looks like. You’ll be our first design leader and will build the Design function from the ground up. You’ll establish the principles, systems, and standards that shape every GovWell product—while remaining deeply hands-on in the work. You’ll redesign the look and feel of our core platform, help us create AI experiences that feel integral rather than bolted on, and give engineers the tools to build polished, consistent products without design becoming a bottleneck. This is not a role for someone who wants to inherit a mature team or spend most of their time reviewing other people’s work. Initially, you’ll be a full-time individual contributor and thought leader. Over time, you’ll hire and lead the team needed to make design a lasting competitive advantage for GovWell. This role reports directly to our CTO and Co-Founder, Ben Cohen https://www.linkedin.com/in/bencohen5/. We have a hybrid work culture that combines regular in-person collaboration at our New York City office (3+ days per week) with flexibility to work remotely. ☀️ WHY GOVWELL? - A mission that matters: Building AI-powered products to fix outdated government systems isn’t just a design challenge—it’s a historic opportunity to improve our foundational relationship with government and ensure trillions of tax dollars result in high-quality services. WATCH: Mission & Vision with CEO & Co-Founder Troy LeCaire https://www.loom.com/share/3d733b22ca0d4fa6be241e0cdd36311a - A rare design problem: Local governments run some of the most complex workflows in the economy. Your job will be to make that complexity feel simple without stripping away the power that public servants need. - Real-world impact: GovWell is the system of record for government services affecting millions of Americans. From helping a small business open sooner to accelerating the construction of affordable housing, your work will make an immediate difference. - The chance to define the standard: Our product is established and growing, but our design language is still taking shape. You won’t be maintaining someone else’s system—you’ll define what exceptional government software looks and feels like. - Join a startup in hyper-growth: We’ve found product-market fit and are scaling quickly, with 4X ARR growth in the last year. You’ll work closely with the founders and have exceptional autonomy, ownership, and influence over the company’s direction. 🎨 WHAT YOU’LL DO - Set the design vision for GovWell. Define the principles that make our products intuitive, differentiated, and unmistakably GovWell. - Reimagine the core product experience. Lead a significant evolution of our platform’s visual design and interaction patterns without losing sight of the complex workflows our customers depend on. - Design AI-native experiences. Shape how AI helps government staff complete work—not as a chatbot bolted onto existing software, but as a cohesive part of the product. - Build our design system. Create the components, patterns, and guidance that let product and engineering teams move quickly while maintaining a consistently high bar. - Stay close to customers. Develop a deep understanding of government staff, residents, contractors, and business owners, then turn their needs into simple and thoughtful product experiences. - Raise the quality of everything we ship. Partner closely with our CTO, Head of Data (Max Payson https://www.linkedin.com/in/max-payson-08328b99/ - former Principal Engineer at Esri), incoming Head of Engineering, and software engineers from early exploration through implementation, sweating the details that separate functional software from a truly great product. - Build the Design function from 0 to 1. Define how design operates at GovWell, then hire and develop a world-class team as the company grows. 🧠 WHO YOU ARE - Complexity, made simple: You have a track record of designing intuitive, beautiful products for complex use cases. - A player, not just a coach: You’re an exceptional hands-on product designer who can take an ambiguous problem through to a polished experience—and you’re excited to do the work yourself. - More than a pair of hands: You have strong product judgment. You challenge assumptions, simplify workflows, and help determine what should be built—not just how requirements should look. - AI-native, not AI-curious: You’re an active user of AI and have thoughtful, evolving opinions about how it should reshape software experiences. - Systems without bureaucracy: You can establish a design system that helps teams move faster without letting the system become more important than the product. - Clarity creates momentum: You communicate clearly and can bring founders, product managers, engineers, and customers along with your thinking. - Vision down to the last pixel: You move comfortably between articulating a multi-year product vision and debating the right label, state, or interaction. - A builder of teams: You want to create a Design function and eventually lead a team, but you’re energized by starting as a hands-on individual contributor. - Empathy without prerequisites: You can deeply understand the needs of government staff and residents without prior govtech experience. - Values are how you operate: You align closely with our Core Values https://govwell.com/careers#core-values. 🖥️ DESIGN TOOLING - Lovable - Cursor - Figma 💸 COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS Compensation within the posted salary band will be commensurate with experience. All offers will include: - Competitive base salary. - Equity / stock options. - Medical, dental, and vision insurance. - 401(k) program. - Flexible PTO. ➡️ CLICK HERE TO MEET THE ENGINEERING TEAM https://govwell.com/team?departments_equal=Product Below: a picture of the entire GovWell team celebrating our Series A with a boat cruise on the Hudson! jobs.title: Founding Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT ARINI Arini is building the single platform to run all healthcare operations. Healthcare has spent the last decade consolidating under large enterprises, but operations are still fragmented, manual, and expensive. A large group runs dozens of disconnected systems for scheduling, billing, insurance, accounts payable, and reporting, with people moving data between them by phone, fax, and spreadsheet. Outpatient healthcare is a $650 billion market, and almost every dollar of it still runs on manual work. Consolidators bought thousands of clinics on the promise that scale would expand margins and lift their EBITDA multiple. Scale alone has not delivered it. Automation is now the only way to hit the numbers they promised investors, and Arini is how they get there. We partner with some of the largest healthcare enterprises in the country, covering thousands of clinics and billions of dollars in annual revenue. We ship the systems that run their operations end to end, and the best of that work becomes the platform that scales across enterprises. When operations run themselves, patients feel it: calls answered on the first ring, appointments booked in seconds, insurance sorted before they walk in, and clinicians who spend their day on care instead of paperwork. That is what we are building, for every clinic in the country. We are backed by Y Combinator (W24) and on track to grow more than tenfold in 2026. THE TEAM Everyone at Arini ships code, including operators, growth, and customer leads. Our founders, Rami and Abdul, have worked together for over a decade. Rami studied computer science at MIT, Abdul at Harvard. Everyone carries more than one job, and nobody has time for work that does not matter. If AI can do it, a person should not be doing it. We move extremely fast and take extreme ownership. THE ROLE You will design the products that run operations for the largest healthcare enterprises in the country. Our forward deployed engineers find the problems inside each customer, and our software engineers build the systems that solve them. You make sure the people who depend on those systems love using them. That is three groups of people: front desk staff who work alongside our agents every day, operators at headquarters who run hundreds to thousands of locations, and our own FDEs who stand up a new enterprise in weeks. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Shadow operators at every level, from the front desk of a clinic to regional managers to C-suite executives. Combine what you learn with requirements from engineering and data on how our products are actually used, and design something that holds up to all three. - Design the products operators at multi-billion dollar healthcare enterprises use every day, working directly with the FDEs who build them: business intelligence and reporting across thousands of clinic locations, agents that automate accounting, procurement, insurance verification, and more. - Decide how our agents show their work. What a person sees after an agent books an appointment, flags an invoice for review, or hands off a call it could not handle. - Prototype in code. Use Figma when it helps, but expect to build in Cursor or Claude Code and ship small changes yourself. - Build the design system our engineers and growth team use, so they ship good interfaces without waiting on you. jobs.title: Product Designer, Design Systems
jobs.descriptionText: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Design at Anthropic sits at the intersection of craft, research, and product intuition. Design systems is a growing team working on products that millions of people use daily, and on interactions that don't have established conventions yet. Our work shapes how people experience AI: whether Claude feels like a tool or a collaborator, whether it earns trust or erodes it. We partner closely with engineers and researchers, often designing around capabilities that are emerging in real time. That means staying close to the models, prototyping rapidly, and being comfortable with ambiguity. We care deeply about the details that make something feel polished, trustworthy and human. We ship fast and learn in the open. We'd rather get something in front of users and iterate than wait for perfection. The Design Systems team exists to define and elevate the language of our UI and core interactions. Every Claude product, from claude.ai to Claude Code, shares one system, including the guidance Claude itself follows when it generates UI. You would be joining an early-stage team, working with design engineers and product designers across the company. You may be a good fit if you: Are as comfortable designing on canvas tools as you are building and prototyping within the product, and prefer to ship in days, not months. Have worked on design systems that balance simplicity with creative flair to produce beautiful products out of the box. Care about the smallest details as much as the big picture, from a pixel to how the whole app fits together. Make the people around you better through sharp, kind feedback and low ego. Get up to speed quickly and can make an impact on projects already in motion. Key responsibilities Design and evolve the system, from foundations (colour, type, spacing, icons, tokens, theming) to components like menus, dialogs, sidebars and the chat composer. Design the expressive layer as a system, not one-offs: motion, illustration and icons that are brand and system at once. Make the system legible to Claude as well as people: the guidance, metadata and evals that show whether Claude uses it correctly. Partner with product teams: help designers and engineers apply the system well, and feed recurring gaps back into the system. Prototype in code and ship: land changes in the design-system package alongside engineers, using Claude Code in your own practice. Minimum qualifications Strong visual and interaction craft. Experience building or working on a design system. Experience with design tokens, theming and accessibility standards. Fluency in whichever tool gets an idea across fastest, from Figma to code. Preferred qualifications Experience building products at the highest level of craft. Has shipped voice or other beyond-the-screen work, with native mobile instincts. Has designed an icon set, illustration style or motion system used across products. Experience defining evals, lint rules or automated checks for UI quality. 8+ years of product design experience. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $305,000 — $385,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.descriptionText: HEALTH CAN’T WAIT. Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t. Alan exists to end the wait. Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way. So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience. We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture https://alan.com/en/careers. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR. Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. Our goal is simple: build the most member-centric health experience there is, with high standards of craft and a real understanding of the people we design for. We are growing fast, and AI is changing what is possible in the way we work. We are looking for someone who loves tooling, ops and AI to help us move faster without lowering the bar on quality. This is a builder role where design, operations and AI meet. You will scope where AI and automation can help us build faster, scale better and catch quality issues earlier, then turn the best ideas into tools the community actually uses. Along the way, you will help us improve our rituals and best practices, and share what we learn inside and outside Alan. You are not a designer or a researcher yourself: you are the enabler that allows the community to go faster and perform better as our member base grows. 🤝 YOUR MISSIONS You will help D&R work smarter and keep quality high as we grow, in close collaboration with the community, its lead, and the engineering, Product Ops and platform teams we work with. You will help shape our community strategy on AI and tooling, then build and run what comes out of it. - Explore: Test new AI tools and automations, find the ones that really save time or improve quality, and share the best with the community. Work with our internal AI tooling teams to bring what’s cutting edge to design and research. - Build: Create skills, agents and automated checks that make design and research work more efficient, reliable and of higher quality. - Run the tooling: Maintain and upgrade the tools the community relies on, and be our point of contact with Alan’s platform and agentic teams. - Improve how we work: Bring in better practices and rituals, push our existing rituals to the next level and help us show what we learn and achieve, inside and outside Alan. - Own your roadmap: Identify opportunities, prioritize solutions, set clear goals, track adoption and quality, and adjust as you go. 🚀 YOU ARE A GOOD FIT IF... You are an ops-minded builder with around 4 years of experience in ops or enablement roles: design ops, tooling, automation, analytics, program management or something close. Design and research interests you, but what drives you is helping teams work better with tools, automation and better rituals. What you bring - Hands-on experience automating work. You have replaced repetitive tasks with automations, internal tools or AI workflows (no-code, low-code or AI tools), at work or on your own projects, and you can tell us what you built and who used it. - Familiarity with AI tools. You have built or tested skills, agents or automations, and you care that they are reliable, not just impressive in a demo. - Comfort working with engineers. You can build things yourself, you know when to ask for production-grade work, and you speak their language. - Experience supporting a team or community, for example through onboarding, rituals, events or internal communications. - Strong English communication, to collaborate with our international team. French is a plus. Nice to have - Experience in or alongside a design or research team. - Familiarity with Figma and design systems. Qualities we look for - Builder and strategic mindset: you make progress with incomplete information, choose the simplest approach that works, and ship. - Rigour: you set a baseline and a target, and improve with each iteration. - Systems thinking: you see how people, processes, tools and data fit together. - Judgment: you frame ambiguous problems, prioritise, and know what to drop. - Clear communication: you keep people updated and explain your choices. 🌍 WHERE YOU CAN BE BASED Location: Based in Paris, France 🎯 IMPORTANT NOTE: WE HIRE PEOPLE, NOT ROLES If you’re excited about this opportunity but don’t check every box, we’d love to hear from you. If you identify yourself as a woman: Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements? Remember, this is just a guide, not a checklist. We’ll be thrilled to receive your application! 🔖 Check out our About Alan https://alan.com/about and Career https://alan.com/careers pages, as well as our Medium https://medium.com/alan, blog https://blog.alan.com/ and Glassdoor https://www.glassdoor.com/Overview/Working-at-Alan-EI_IE1696043.11,15.htm page for more info. 👀 READ MORE ABOUT ALAN 🙌 Perks & Benefits https://alan.com/en/careers/a/salary-equity: Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers. 🤘 A strong culture https://alan.com/en/about/a/leadership-principles: People joining Alan are often surprised and delighted by our innovative working method. jobs.descriptionText: Perplexity is looking for a Content Designer to shape the words across our products. You'll design the language people see and hear across our family of Perplexity apps, from the first screen of onboarding to the way an agent explains what it's doing. Fundamentally, we are all writers. Our product is primarily spoken language and written product; but as we scale, we want someone who will continue to work on clarity, usefulness, and keep it unmistakably Perplexity. You're a designer first? You're an engineer first? You're a writer first? Your shape is not conventional, and you wear many hats. You are fluent in AI tooling. You have strong UX fundamentals and good product instincts. You use language to solve product problems: flows, naming, information architecture, error states, permissions, and moments where people need to trust what the product is telling them. You command words. You command agents, and make decisions about words. You can write one perfect line, and you can build the system that keeps thousands of lines consistent. You'll sit on the Design Systems team and work closely with product designers, engineers, PMs, research, brand, and marketing. (Again) You're fluent in AI-powered tools and use it every day. You understand how models behave, how prompts and system instructions shape what people see, and how to define and judge quality when the output isn't fully deterministic. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design and write in-product language across web, mobile, desktop, and voice, including UI copy, flows, onboarding, notifications, empty states, errors, and in-product education - Partner with product designers from the start of a project, shaping flows, structure, and information architecture as well as the words in them - Name features and products, and own terminology, navigation labels, and taxonomies so the product stays easy to understand as it grows - Make complex AI and agent behavior understandable, including what the product is doing, why, what it can't do, and when it needs a person's input - Shape how AI-generated content reads by writing and refining prompts and system instructions, and help define voice and response style for our models in product - Define content quality standards and help build evaluation criteria, datasets, and reviewer guidance for AI-generated content - Build and maintain voice and tone guidelines, content patterns, and content guidance in our design system so every team can write well - Use research, data, and experiments to test language and improve comprehension, activation, and task completion - Partner with brand and marketing so product language and our external voice feel like one company - Work with internationalization partners so the product reads well in every language we support - Review copy in code and ship small language changes directly when it's the fastest path WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 5+ years of experience in content design, UX writing, or product design, shipping software at scale - An excellent portfolio that shows how your language shaped product decisions, with clear before and after examples and your role in each - Strong UX fundamentals, including interaction design, information architecture, usability, and accessibility - Good product sensibility and judgment about what to build, what to cut, and what matters most to people - Exceptional writing and editing skills, with range from precise interface copy to clear explanations and confident naming - Strong AI fluency, including hands-on experience writing prompts, working with LLMs, and judging the quality of AI-generated content - Systems thinking, with experience building content frameworks, style guides, or terminology that scale across teams - Clear communication, with the ability to explain content decisions and tradeoffs to designers, engineers, and leaders - You care about shipping great software more than anything else NICE TO HAVE - Experience designing content for AI products, assistants, agents, or conversational interfaces - Experience with prompt engineering, model evals, or working with research teams on model behavior - Experience across consumer and enterprise products, including admin, permissions, privacy, and billing flows - Comfort working in code, such as editing strings, reviewing PRs, or prototyping with AI tools - Experience with localization and writing for global audiences NOTES FOR CANDIDATES We want to see portfolio work where your words changed the product. Show us the problem, the options you explored, the language you shipped, and what happened after. We value end-to-end ownership, range, and impact, and we'd love to see examples of AI-related work, such as prompts, evaluations, or content you designed for model output.

jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT WATERSHED Watershed https://watershed.com/ is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team. We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us! THE ROLE To run a sustainable business, our customers need climate insights at their fingertips. That’s where great design comes in — we are building powerful software that enables the biggest companies in the world to measure their carbon footprint with ease, and drive change across their organization. We are hiring a Product designer to join our AI Products group. Product designers at Watershed partner closely with product and engineering from vision through execution, painting the big picture and sweating the details. We’re experts in our customers goals and pain points, and drive constant iteration to get the right solution in hand to meet their needs. As designers we push each other to perfect our craft and uplevel the outcome, treasuring our weekly jams and crits. And working in sustainability, you’ll build domain expertise in one of the most critical and motivating problem spaces. In this role you will: - Own design end-to-end on one of our AI Products teams, like Product Footprints https://watershed.com/solutions/product-footprints or AI Platform https://watershed.com/en-GB/platform/sustainability-ai, helping supercharge sustainability teams to focus their efforts where it counts – whether that’s on automating away the data wrangling to measure their footprints, driving sustainability insights, or improving the environment impact of their physical goods via ROI-positive supply chain decisions. - Design and ship complex AI product – bringing UX thinking to design decisions inclusive of data models and systems, prompts and evals, and user interfaces. - Drive deep discovery to uncover new product opportunities. Use customer feedback and product analytics to iterate quickly and move meaningful product and business metrics - Build the vision and product strategy to bring the next chapter of product to life - Partner closely with engineering, product, and design teams to execute, and go-to-market teams to understand and build for customers. - Leverage AI throughout your design process, as well as in the product itself, to deliver great outcomes You might be a fit if you: - Have 5+ years experience designing software, preferably at enterprise software companies or in technical/complex problem spaces. Bonus if you have experience working in the sustainability or supply chain domains. - Have a knack for in-the-weeds systems thinking and a love for rapid, 0-1 product building - Have a track record shipping powerful and intuitive product experiences that customers love - Are proficient in design craft fundamentals — consistently demonstrating solid design process, strong interaction craft, and an eye for polish - Have shipped AI products, and are proficient using AI tools to aid discovery, synthesis, and design execution - Are customer obsessed and excited to spend time with users and prospects - Are enthusiastic about product and business ownership — you are excited to go deep on climate and become an expert on the market’s paths forward - Want to join a startup, take responsibility for the fate of the company, and move fast - Prior experience in the climate space is not necessary Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles) Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so. What’s the interview process like? It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process. What if I need accommodations for my interview? At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

jobs.title: User Experience Designer: Hardware Systems
jobs.descriptionText: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About You and The Role The New Products team is seeking a User Experience Designer to research and shape how people interact with Zipline’s precision delivery system, Platform 2. This cross-disciplinary role sits at the intersection of industrial design, software, operations, and service design. You will focus on the human experience of our hardware and the digital tools that support them. You will own the definition of design requirements for system touchpoints and champion them through all phases of development to enable the best experiences for Zipline operators and customers. What You'll Do Design end-to-end user experiences across physical and digital touchpoints, including aircraft, pods, docks, loading workflows, partner infrastructure, operator tools, and customer-facing moments. Translate complex system behavior into clear interaction models, user journeys, service flows, and product requirements. Partner with Engineers and Industrial Designers to define physical interactions, affordances, feedback, status communication, and error recovery. Work with Digital Product teams to ensure consistency between physical systems behavior and software interfaces. Conduct field research with operators, partners, customers, technicians, and internal teams to understand real-world workflows and pain points. Identify design opportunities across system hardware, software, service, and operations. Help prioritize user needs and translate them into product requirements. Prototype and test interaction concepts quickly, using whatever fidelity is appropriate: sketches, diagrams, click-through prototypes, physical mockups, or in-field simulations. Advocate for clarity, safety, usability, and human trust in autonomous delivery experiences. What You'll Bring Minimum 5+ years of experience in User Experience, Industrial Design, Service / Interaction Design, or Product Design shaping user connection to physical products, digital interfaces, and real-world workflows. A strong portfolio beautifully showcasing real-world results. Strong visual communication skills, including journey maps, diagrams, wireframes, storyboards, and prototypes. A practical, simplicity-seeking design sensibility and an ability to prototype physically and digitally - beautifully. A high degree of comfort presenting work to executive leadership and acting as the champion for product requirements and design decisions. Strong systems thinking and the ability to make complex technical experiences simple and usable. Design Research acumen: conducting in-person analysis of user behavior through interviews, field visits, focus groups and surveys Ability to move between abstract journey-level thinking and detailed interaction design that are easily understandable by teams who will implement them. Ability to work in ambiguous, fast-moving environments with evolving technical constraints. Entrepreneurial mindset and a humble confidence backed by real-world understanding. What Else You Need To Know The starting cash range for this role is $153,000 - $210,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; overtime pay; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply! Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT US Tavus http://tavus.io/ is an AI research lab pioneering human computing. We’re building PALs: a new kind of application that closes the gap between people and machines, free from the friction of today’s systems. Our real-time human simulation models let machines see, hear, respond, and even look real—enabling meaningful, face-to-face conversations. PALs combine the emotional intelligence of humans with the reach and reliability of machines, making them capable, trusted agents available 24/7, in every language, on our terms. Imagine a therapist anyone can afford. A personal trainer that adapts to your schedule. A fleet of medical assistants that can give every patient the attention they need. With Tavus, individuals, enterprises, and developers can all build PALs to connect, understand, and act with empathy at scale. We’re a Series B company backed by world-class investors including Sequoia Capital, Y Combinator, and Scale Venture Partners. Be part of shaping a future where humans and machines truly understand each other. THE ROLE We are seeking a craft-obsessed, systems-minded Product Designer to evolve our product suite and own & grow the Tavus design systems – the components, tokens, and patterns that every surface we build on top of depends on. This is a Product Design role that demands exceptional VisD skills and experience. We need someone with exceptional eye and hand for typography, color, spacing, and detail, who can bring real motion craft to how our system feels in use. But the design system doesn't exist in a vacuum: It has to hold up under real product and UX problems, across a growing portfolio of products, so strong product design judgment is a must. This role has a deliberate arc. In the near term, your focus will be the design system: consolidating, architecting, and elevating it into something stable, distinct, and built to scale with us. As that foundation matures, we expect this role to evolve into ownership of a product area, where you'll carry the same craft and judgment forward into shipping product day to day. We're looking for someone genuinely excited by both halves. You will collaborate closely with product, engineering, and leadership in a fast-paced environment to make the system the clear, trusted foundation for how we design and build. Join our small, creative team of designers, engineers, and product enthusiasts dedicated to thoughtfully bridging the human-machine divide. We're doing it right, sweating the details, and we're in it together. This role is based in the San Francisco Bay Area. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Architect for scale: Define the token architecture, component structure, and theming model (light, dark, and beyond) that let the system flex across products and surfaces without forking or drifting. - Own governance, not just files: Establish the standards, documentation, and contribution model that keep the system coherent as more designers and engineers touch it. Be the clear, decisive voice when tradeoffs get contentious. - Partner deeply with engineering: Work hand-in-hand with frontend engineers to ensure the system is implemented faithfully and effectively. - Elevate craft everywhere: Bring meticulous visual and interaction craft, including motion and micro-interaction detail, to every component and pattern so the system doesn't just function, it feels intentional and distinctly Tavus. “Good enough” isn’t. - Drive adoption: Make the system easier to use than not using it. Build the artifacts, documentation, and relationships that get other designers, engineers, and marketers to reach for the system first. WHO YOU ARE - An indefatigable visual designer, with an exceptional, well-trained eye for typography, color, layout, and detail, plus real motion design chops. - A genuinely capable product designer, with 6+ years of experience and solid UX judgment. You understand user flows, interaction patterns, and product tradeoffs well enough that your systems hold up with elegance under real product pressure. - Experienced building and governing design systems at scale. You can point to a system you've architected and evolved, not just contributed to, with bonus points for work both within an existing component framework as well as from-scratch builds. - Original, not just tasteful. We're not looking for someone who can recognize good design when they see it; we're looking for someone who can produce something distinct that hasn't been seen before. If your portfolio could pass for a dozen other SaaS products, this isn't the right fit. We'll ask you to walk us through specific decisions and the reasoning behind them, and the results those decisions yielded. - Principled and able to defend it. You’re especially adept at articulating why a decision is correct. You push back on your own instincts as readily as you push back on others'. - Decisive in ambiguity: You don't need permission to make a call. When a system decision has no clean answer, you weigh the tradeoffs, make a defensible choice, and move, while staying meticulous about the details within that decision. - Technically fluent: You're comfortable working close to code: reviewing implementation, catching and stopping drift between design and build, and speaking the language of the engineers who ship your system. - Built for startup pace: You can operate with minimal specs and shifting priorities, protecting the highest quality bar while moving fast. BENEFITS & CULTURE When you join Tavus, you’re joining a diverse and supportive team. Our work is driven by our people, and our success is shared by all. This position has a flexible work schedule, unlimited PTO, competitive healthcare, and gear stipends, as well as plenty of fun. At the end of the day, we want Tavus to be a place for you to learn, directly drive impact, and work with a team you love. To learn more about our team culture and benefits, check out our hiring page. https://www.tavus.io/careers Tavus is growing fast, and we’d like you to grow with us. If you’re excited to get your hands dirty and help make machines more human, drop your resume and we’ll be in touch. We are not looking for cultural fits, we are looking for culture creators. Diversity is what drives our success – it’s at the core of how we hire, communicate, and work. We are inclusive to all and combine our diverse backgrounds, skill sets, and perspectives to build the best experiences for our clients.

jobs.title: Product Designer, Docs & Learning
jobs.descriptionText: Thank you for considering Tailscale. If this job description resonates with you, please apply. Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic! About Tailscale Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital. About the Role We're looking for a Product Designer with experience designing for technical documentation to join the Tailscale product design team. You will work as a designer dedicated to the Docs team focusing on information architecture of the site, presentation of content, and educational support materials. At Tailscale, we don’t see Documentation as an afterthought; it’s how users learn, deploy, troubleshoot, and fall in love with Tailscale. It’s both a discovery surface and a place where users look to find answers in stressful situations. This designer will work closely with dedicated engineers on the Docs site to ensure the quality and delivery of content meets the needs of all users. They will collaborate with technical writers, product designers, engineers, PMs, and customer-facing colleagues to ensure documentation is intuitive, visually compelling, and deeply user centric. Key Responsibilities Some examples of projects we anticipate in the near term: Support a transition from our current docs platform to a new one, including appropriate IA changes for a large docs corpus. Establish a brand-appropriate style guide for the new docs site that optimizes for readability. Draft and maintain a library of diagrams to be used as assets within the docs site and educational content. Enable experimentation on docs surfaces through collaboration with the growth team and test-related tooling. Design educational content for LMS materials with attention to classroom usability. What We Are Looking For 5+ years of product design experience, including complex work you've owned end-to-end (portfolio required) Experience with technically sophisticated B2B or infrastructure applications A portfolio that shows how you've made technical content clear, usable, and visually engaging Experience adapting brand guidelines to documentation and educational content Proven success working in a distributed, async environment Mindset and Approach You think of documentation as a product, not a deliverable: you ask what users need, test your assumptions, and iterate You're comfortable with technical subject matter—networking, infrastructure, security. You don't need to be an expert, but you're curious and willing to learn You communicate complex ideas clearly through layout, diagram, example, and plain language You're collaborative and low-ego, working directly with engineers and technical writers who bring their own approaches You use data and feedback to guide decisions, and you hold strong opinions about what makes documentation work You run your own workload, shift between projects as priorities change, and don't need someone else to tell you what matters You have a confident point of view on users and product quality—and the initiative to act on it Nice to Have Front-end literacy (HTML/CSS) to collaborate effectively on implementation Experience with static site generators (we use a custom Markdown setup) Familiarity with networking or infrastructure concepts (VPNs, DNS, firewalls, routing) Experience with AI-assisted design or content tools Experience designing developer-facing documentation (technical guides, reference material, troubleshooting, tutorials) As a company, we strive to maintain fair and equitable compensation practices within our team across all roles and all levels. Tailscale's compensation package includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. The salary range displayed on each job posting represents the target range for a new hire's base salary. Individual offers may vary based on experience and skill set. US Pay Range $146,000 — $183,000 USD What We Offer An inclusive, flexible environment where you can be your authentic self. We recognize the impact of diverse voices and backgrounds on the growth of our people, product, and company. And that flexibility in how and when you work empowers our team to integrate work and life. A competitive total compensation package. This includes a base salary, an equity incentive plan and variable commission (for quota-based roles). Comprehensive group benefits with no waiting period. Take advantage of coverage for health, vision, dental, and more for you and your family! Remote first company —most of our teams work fully remotely. Enjoy a change of scenery wherever you can get wifi, participate in virtual and in-person social events, and leverage our corporate co-working program to visit WeWork (or other similar spaces near you). Some roles require in-office collaboration depending on team needs, which will be clearly noted in the job description. Employer-funded retirement contributions. Tailscale will match your retirement contributions dollar-for-dollar, up to a maximum annual employer contribution equal to 0.75% of your eligible compensation. Connect with other Tailscalars IRL. Attend our annual company retreat, participate in team off-sites, and collaborate in person with teammates across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Singapore. We support intentional in-person connection through team travel and distributed collaboration. Support for your personal and professional development. Grow your career thoughtfully with $1500 USD annually for professional development, or take advantage of mentorship, coaching, and internal promotion opportunities. Paid time off and a healthy work-life integration. Our flexible, paid time off program supports you for any situation life throws your way, whether moving homes or travelling the world! A build-your-own home office setup. You choose your own company-owned laptop (Mac or PC), receive a monthly home internet reimbursement, and $500 USD to customize your workstation to make it your own. Paid parental leave program . We care about your life outside of work and encourage new parents to take advantage of parental leave top-ups (20 weeks for birthing parents, 16 weeks for non-birthing parents). Tailscale is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive hiring process. If you require an accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process or related to any aspect of this role, please contact your recruiter. Our hiring process uses AI-assisted tools to help screen and assess candidates. All hiring decisions are made by people. Please be aware that legitimate emails from Tailscale's talent team will only originate from @tailscale.com, @greenhouse.io, and @interviews.modernloop.io email addresses. For more information about protecting yourself from impersonators and scams, please visit https://tailscale.com/scam-awareness .
