jobs.title: Lead AI Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: Who We Are HP IQ is HP’s new AI innovation lab. Combining startup agility with HP’s global scale, we’re building intelligent technologies that redefine how the world works, creates, and collaborates. We’re assembling a diverse, world-class team—engineers, designers, researchers, and product minds—focused on creating an intelligent ecosystem across HP’s portfolio. Together, we’re developing intuitive, adaptive solutions that spark creativity, boost productivity, and make collaboration seamless. We create breakthrough solutions that make complex tasks feel effortless, teamwork more natural, and ideas more impactful—always with a human-centric mindset. By embedding AI advancements into every HP product and service, we’re expanding what’s possible for individuals, organisations, and the future of work. Join us as we reinvent work, so people everywhere can do their best work. We're seeking a Lead AI Product Designer to join our Design Team, focused on inventing how AI-powered devices can learn about and assist our users. You'll alternate between deep exploratory work and shipping features that will fundamentally change how people interact with technology. You will architect complex AI-powered systems and craft interfaces that proactively anticipate user needs. Success in this role requires a proven track record of bringing creative AI vision to life through the technical validation of concepts using cutting-edge AI technologies. You'll have the space to explore challenging problems while maintaining a clear focus on shipping products that work. Our goal is to create technology that feels obvious once you experience it. We're looking for designers who can envision a world where AI computing enhances our human capabilities rather than demanding our attention. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds who are excited to help reshape how humans and computers work together. What you might do Lead the definition of AI experiences across HP IQ, setting design direction and taking concepts from exploration through to shipped products. Build high-fidelity, functional prototypes of ambient, multimodal and generative interfaces that adapt to people’s behavior across devices. Shape information architecture for AI-first systems, including how people inspect, edit and control what AI remembers about them. Define when AI should act proactively, ask for input or leave control with the user. Make its behavior understandable, give people ways to correct or undo its actions, and handle delays or inaccurate outputs gracefully. Work with AI research scientists, designers and engineers to test concepts using emerging models and LLM pipelines, and bring promising ideas into production. Essential qualifications 5+ years of digital product design experience, with a proven track record of shipping products Strong ability to code or vibe-code and deploy custom interfaces (SwiftUI, Python, JavaScript, or Origami). You must be fluent in incorporating modern AI-first IDEs and agents (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code) to fluidly bridge visual design and code - Figma-only workflows alone will not suffice. Deep, proven experience building and shipping production-level AI technologies (particularly LLMs and Agentic workflows) in professional product environments Portfolio demonstrating novel approaches to complex interaction problems and non-deterministic outputs Ability to balance exploratory design work with practical implementation constraints Strong systems thinking skills and ability to design for emergent behaviors Enthusiasm for building intuitive, empathetic technology that keeps the human-in-the-loop Curiosity for learning new technologies and finding unexpected solutions to complex problems Preferred skills A passion for tinkering and experimentation Background in information architecture or knowledge management systems Understanding of machine learning best practices and their practical, scalable applications in building intelligence-first UIs Experience designing products that learn from people’s behavior Interest in cognitive science and how humans process/organize information We request that you submit a presentation (Keynote, PDF or Figma preferred) of 1-2 examples of your work, along with any passion projects that you feel represent you as a designer. We’d love to learn how you think about AI in the context of product design, from the experience of using an AI-powered product to its look and feel, the craft behind it, and the trade-offs you made to ship. jobs.descriptionText: From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven. About Us Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data. Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on. Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions. As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact. During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites. About the Role Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies. We're looking for a strategic, hands-on Staff Web Designer who loves solving complex UX challenges, building scalable systems, and turning ideas into real experiences. This role is ideal for a scrappy, systems-minded designer who thrives on ownership, enjoys getting into the details, and is excited to be the primary designer shaping Fivetran's web experiences. You will own the design strategy and hands-on execution for fivetran.com and getdbt.com, building scalable design systems that balance consistency with flexibility. You'll choose when to use existing patterns, when to evolve them, and when a unique experience calls for something new. To bring your projects to life, you will partner closely with Web Strategy, Web Engineering, Brand, Growth Marketing, Product Marketing, and Product teams. Success in this role requires balancing big-picture systems thinking with a willingness to roll up your sleeves. You should be comfortable moving between strategy, wireframes, prototypes, and design systems, making thoughtful trade-offs to ship high-quality work quickly. You will champion AI-powered tools and new ways of working, create scalable processes that reduce repetitive work, and help shape how web design operates as the business grows. We're looking for someone resourceful, opinionated, curious, and energized by building and thinking in systems. You will build the foundations that make great web experiences easier to create, evolve, and scale. This is a full-time position based out of our Oakland office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration, including two days in the office each week to connect and build as a team. Technologies You’ll Use Figma Webflow Sanity Claude Codex Jira Google Analytics (GA4) Amplitude Microsoft Clarity What You’ll Do Own the end-to-end design strategy and execution for Fivetran and dbt, translating complex web strategy into scalable design systems from concept through launch. Operate as the sole web designer, independently driving high-impact initiatives with a scrappy, pragmatic mindset that balances speed, quality, and technical feasibility. Shape and evolve the design systems that power our website, including reusable components, design standards, and interaction patterns that improve consistency and accelerate time to market. Lead AI innovation for web design, experimenting with emerging tools and building repeatable workflows that accelerate prototyping, production, and implementation. Partner closely with web strategy to connect designs to business outcomes and with web engineering to translate designs into real experiences. Champion user-centered design, leveraging user research and competitive insights to identify opportunities and influence web strategy. Serve as a trusted design partner across Growth Marketing, Product Marketing, Brand, Product, and Engineering, challenging assumptions and building alignment around user-centered solutions. Establish high standards for usability, interaction, accessibility, and responsive design, creating reusable guidance and documentation that enable quality at scale. Proactively improve how the web team operates by anticipating risks, removing bottlenecks, and introducing lightweight processes that make execution faster and more effective. Communicate design strategy and outcomes with clarity to influence stakeholders and executive leadership. Skills We’re Looking For Extensive experience in web, product, or UX design, with a proven track record of independently leading high-impact digital experiences from strategy through launch. Exceptional systems thinking, with the ability to simplify complex problems, design scalable information architecture, and create reusable patterns that work across multiple experiences and use cases. Proven experience building and evolving design systems, component libraries, and scalable design frameworks. Deep expertise in UX and interaction design, including user flows, navigation, responsive design, accessibility, wireframing, and high-fidelity prototyping. Experience leveraging AI-powered tools for design, prototyping, design-to-code workflows, or workflow automation, with a strong interest in building more efficient and scalable ways of working. Strong technical fluency and understanding of modern web development, with the ability to collaborate closely with engineers, evaluate implementation trade-offs, and contribute hands-on to bringing designs to life. A resourceful execution mindset with demonstrated success operating independently, navigating ambiguity, prioritizing effectively, and shipping high-quality work in fast-moving environments. Exceptional cross-functional communication and influence, with the confidence to challenge assumptions, articulate design decisions, and align stakeholders. Bonus Skills​ Experience designing for B2B SaaS, enterprise software, developer tools, or data products. Experience working as a solo designer, building design practices and systems from the ground up. Curiosity about emerging web technologies, technical product experiences, and new approaches to designing and building for the web. Strong business acumen, with the ability to leverage behavioral analytics, user research, and experimentation to inform decisions and improve user journeys. Familiarity with experimentation, conversion rate optimization, and behavioral analytics tools such as Optimizely, GA4, Amplitude, or Microsoft Clarity. jobs.descriptionText: In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. We've scaled beyond the millions of people using Perplexity every day for research, shopping, investing and curiosity into a new paradigm of using AI to transform knowledge into action. ABOUT THE ROLE Perplexity is looking for an experienced Lead Product Designer to own iPhone and Android design on our Native & Mobile team. You'll design how Perplexity lives on the device people carry everywhere, and how that device works with everything else they use: their Mac, their Windows PC, their Linux machine, and the agents doing work on their behalf. Native & Mobile is one team covering every platform we build for. Our agents increasingly run for minutes or hours, on your computer or in the cloud, and the phone becomes the place you start that work, follow its progress, step in when it needs you, and pick up the result. You'll design that relationship between devices so it feels like one product, not a set of separate apps. The best mobile work here goes deep on the platform. You'll design experiences that take full advantage of what each device can do: notifications, Live Activities and the Dynamic Island, widgets, voice, Shortcuts and App Intents, share and system extensions, and their Android counterparts. You'll prototype in the real material, on device, using coding agents to turn ideas into working SwiftUI and shipping changes in the codebase alongside engineers. The role is deeply cross-functional. You'll partner closely with iOS, Android, and desktop engineers, product, and fellow designers across the org, and you care about everything that makes a product great: product thinking, interaction, visual craft, copywriting, and engineering. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Lead product design for our iPhone and Android apps, from early concept through polished, shipped detail - Design how the phone works alongside our desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux, so people can start, monitor, steer, and hand off work across devices without friction - Design for agents that work in the background: progress you can glance at, interruptions that respect attention, and clear moments when a person needs to approve, answer, or take over - Make deep use of native platform capabilities, including notifications, Live Activities, widgets, voice, system intents, and extensions, so Perplexity feels built for each device rather than ported to it - Design trust into the product: permissions, approvals, and privacy flows that are clear and honest, and that keep people in control when an agent acts on their behalf - Prototype on device early and often, using real code to answer questions static mocks can't - Use coding agents to build in the production codebase and put up your own PRs, working alongside engineers to close the gap between the design and what ships - Keep patterns consistent across iOS, Android, and desktop while respecting each platform's conventions - Explore what new platform capabilities, input methods, and form factors make possible - Think about how to go from 0→1, and about how your decisions scale as the product grows - Contribute to process so we're always shipping changes you're proud of, as often as possible WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - A strong track record of shipping native mobile apps for consumer or prosumer products - Deep fluency in iOS: platform conventions, navigation patterns, gestures, system components, and what's new each year - Working knowledge of Android and Material conventions, and the judgment to know when a design should adapt across platforms and when it should stay the same - Experience designing products that span multiple devices, or that integrate deeply with operating system features - Excellent interaction, visual, and motion skills, with a sharp eye for detail at small sizes and in glanceable moments - Comfort building with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar) to prototype on device and land changes in a production codebase. You don't need to be an engineer, but you know enough about SwiftUI and Xcode to direct the work, review what it produces, and know when it's right - Systems thinking: you can turn complex, technical, or asynchronous behavior into something simple and understandable - An excellent communicator who can tell a clear story about design rationale to team members and leadership - You care about shipping great software more than anything else - Comfort with a high level of autonomy and ambiguity, and the craft to be seen as a peer lead by the rest of the design team - 5+ years of industry experience NICE TO HAVE - Experience designing for Android or working in Jetpack Compose - Experience designing for macOS, Windows, or other desktop platforms - Experience designing for AI agents, automation, developer tools, or products where software acts on a person's behalf - Shipped work with Live Activities, widgets, App Intents, watchOS, or other system-level surfaces - You've already been exploring or prototyping interactions for new form factors, like foldables NOTES FOR CANDIDATES - Please submit your portfolio with your application.

jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT US Our mission is to reinvent the way people learn, starting with language. Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages. Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana. ABOUT THE DESIGN TEAM We’re a small and mighty team of five that sit at the intersection of craft, research, invention and product thinking. We build consumer experiences used by millions, alongside B2B products that help organizations bring Speak to their teams. The design work is genuinely novel — inventing how someone talks to an AI tutor, what feedback feels like when you're learning out loud, how a roleplay session should land emotionally, and how you measure a true proficiency score. Our work shapes the future of how people learn with AI and we partner closely with Engineering, Learning Design, Product, and Analytics to do it. We stay close to our users and to how our experiences actually feel by prototyping with AI, testing conversation design and voice interaction, and getting comfortable with ambiguity. Our team takes craft seriously and has a lot of fun doing it — we developed our design principles in a multi-week offsite and iterate on them on a living board in our office. We take language classes together to ground our work in first principles. We stay close to our learners through team trips to Seoul, Tokyo, and Taipei, as well as lighter-touch interviews, surveys, betas, and AB tests. We believe in a critique and build culture with high trust, and also get a bit competitive over ping pong. We have something to prove: that learning products can be both deeply effective and beautifully crafted. If you want to do the most interesting design work of your career, let's talk. ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES As a Product Designer focused on consumer experiences, you’ll design the core moments that help learners build real-world speaking confidence: finding the right path, practicing with AI, getting feedback, staying motivated, and building a lasting learning habit. Speak is inventing new interaction patterns for language learning — from AI tutoring and voice-first practice to roleplay, proficiency measurement, and personalized curriculum. You’ll work across ambiguous, high-impact product areas where interaction design, learning science, AI behavior, and emotional craft all matter. - Shape strategy and end-to-end product experiences for Speak’s consumer learning surfaces, bringing deep empathy for learners across cultures, motivations, and proficiency levels - Design across key growth moments — onboarding, activation, habit formation, retention, and subscription experiences — while protecting learner trust and long-term learning outcomes - Prototype quickly in AI tools, code, or interactive design tools to make new learning experiences feel real before they are fully built - Partner with Product, Data, Research, and Engineering to define opportunities, evaluate impact, and raise the quality bar for learner-facing product work - Use qualitative and quantitative signals to understand learner behavior, synthesize insights, and make strong product judgments - Invent novel interaction patterns for AI-powered learning that go beyond generic AI templates - Thrive in an ambiguous, fast-moving startup environment where the best answer often has to be discovered through making The exact product area you will work on will depend on team needs and your strengths, but likely areas include onboarding, activation, personalized learning, speaking practice, subscriptions, and learner motivation. This role is primarily anchored in our consumer experience, with opportunities to collaborate across adjacent surfaces as Speak grows. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR - 6+ years of product design experience. You have experience designing high-quality consumer products. - You stay close to users. You think about real people learning real languages in real contexts. You actively seek out the humans using the product, not just data about them and are able to synthesize valuable insights about them that inform strategy and direction. You seek ways to put your work in front of people, before you feel it’s perfect just to learn something valuable. - Product thinking and structured judgment. You frame the problem before solving it and always know why you’re doing something. You can distill what you’re working on into simple narrative framings and key beats without being lost in the details. - AI-native workflow. You already use AI creatively in your process to unlock speed and quality and are eager to continue learning how to apply it in novel ways. - Taste and craft while moving fast. You can spot a great idea in a sea of okay ones and understand what’s worth investing in building. You do this while moving quickly and know when to stay scrappy vs invest deeply in final polish. - Communication and stakeholder collaboration. You can own a room, build trust, and push back when something isn't right. You bring people into your work along the way knowing that multiple perspectives produce the strongest work. WE ALSO LOVE TO SEE - Experience in language learning, education, or another domain with deep cross-cultural product surface area - A bias toward prototypes to communicate ideas, test assumptions, and make your thinking tangible - A strong portfolio that demonstrates user-centric thinking, high craft, and innovative interaction patterns - Contributions to design systems that scale beyond a single team - A point of view about agentic workflows you'd be excited to share with our team and ability to tinker directly in code WHY WORK AT SPEAK 1. Join a fantastic, tight-knit team at the right time: we're growing very quickly, we've most recently raised our Series C from some of the top investors in the valley, and we've achieved product-market fit in our initial markets. You'd join at a magical time when a single person could significantly change the course of the company. 2. Do your life's work with people you’ll love working with: we care strongly about our craft and want every person at Speak to feel like they're growing every day. We believe in the idea that working with people you both enjoy and have respect for makes everything better. We hire thoughtfully and only work with people we admire deeply. 3. Global in nature: We're live in over 40 countries and launching in a number of new markets soon. We have dedicated offices in San Francisco, Ljubljana, Seoul, Tokyo, and Taipei, and you’ll have the opportunity to talk to users in each of these regions on a regular basis as well as travel. 4. Impact people's lives in a major way: Learning a language is one of the single most life-changing skills one can learn, and right now 99% of people never achieve their goal because the process is broken. We’re helping millions of people achieve their goals and improve their lives. Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: LiveX AI · Senior Product Designer Palo Alto, CA · Full-time, on-site · Department: Product & Design · Reports to: CEO Source: https://livex.ai/careers/senior-product-designer (posted Oct 9, 2026) ABOUT LIVEX AI LiveX AI builds the human-AI interface for the physical world. Through its AI City work with NVIDIA, people can walk up, talk face-to-face with an AI, and get help in stores, hotels, hospitals, airports, and stadiums. Its 4K full-body AI agents support 140 languages, display products in 3D, give interactive instruction, and run on-prem or in the cloud. Customers include Walmart, PUMA, and the NFL Super Bowl. LiveX handles IP design, hardware, interaction, enterprise AI agents, and deployment in-house. Two form factors, Gateway (freestanding, life-size) and Portal (wall-mounted, shelf edge), share the same experience and content. Early-stage startup. ABOUT THE ROLE Own how LiveX looks, feels, and works: the on-screen characters, the interactions people have with them, and how LiveX is introduced to the public. A hands-on Senior Product Designer with strong visual craft who works across product, brand and campaigns, motion, 3D, and interactive prototypes, taking projects from early concept through finished assets, polished interfaces, and working web prototypes, and shipping them with engineering. RESPONSIBILITIES - Design the human-AI interface: user flows, interfaces, and interactions for Gateway and Portal, covering touch, voice, and content on a life-size screen used by walk-up users in noisy environments. - Shape the characters: develop the look and presence of 4K digital twins and branded characters (mascots, house experts, licensed talent), including how they move, gesture, and present products. - Bring products to life in 3D: product renders, scenes, and animations for on-screen display, launches, ads, and product pages. - Create motion and video: motion graphics; edit product films, demos, and event videos from raw footage to final delivery. - Lead visual design for campaigns and launches: key visuals, posters, trade show graphics, social assets, on-screen content. - Build working prototypes: turn interactive concepts into HTML/CSS/JavaScript web demos, then develop them further with engineering. - Develop AI-assisted creative workflows combining generative image/video tools with professional design and 3D tools. - Contribute original ideas: campaign concepts, product features, new ways people can interact with AI in the physical world. - Maintain a consistent brand across screen, print, digital, video, and 3D. REQUIREMENTS - 5–8 years of professional product design experience, with visual design as a core strength and shipped UX/UI work. - Early-stage startup experience (seed to Series B, under ~50 people), owning design end to end without a design team. - Strong portfolio of published advertising work: campaigns, posters, key visuals. - Proficiency with generative image and video tools, with good judgment about when to use them. - Advanced skills in professional design, motion graphics, and video editing software. - Solid 3D skills: modeling, lighting, materials, rendering, animation. - Hands-on motion design, video graphics, and editing experience. - Can build small web projects independently and hand them off to engineers. - Required: hands-on use of AI coding tools for design and prototyping. - Initiative, creative ownership, and a clear point of view on product and design. - Able to work on-site in Palo Alto; lives in or will relocate to the SF Bay Area. Design taste, visual craft, and product judgment are the most important hiring criteria. NICE-TO-HAVES - Strongly preferred: digital human or virtual avatar experience (character design, real-time avatars, lip-sync, performance capture). - Game art, game UI, or real-time 3D engine work. - UX/UI for touchscreens, voice interfaces, or large-format displays. - End-to-end ownership in a startup or small team. - Modern front-end frameworks or real-time 3D on the web. COMPENSATION Not listed. HOW TO APPLY (ORIGINAL POSTING) Email resume and portfolio to career@livex.ai (subject "Candidate Application - Senior Product Designer"), including advertising/campaign work, 3D renders/animation/motion samples, and at least one self-built web project (live link or repo).

jobs.descriptionText: About the Team At DoorDash, design means making experiences for the people who order, the people who prepare, and the people who deliver. As a Designer at DoorDash, you want to build things that matter to real people. You're at your best when you can move from idea to shipped product quickly, bringing experiences to life that reach and influence users at massive scale. You'll care about whether the product you make solved a real problem for real people, or changed how someone experiences their day. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with Engineering and Product Management, dig into the data, and use LLM-powered tools alongside traditional design tools. If the LLM powered tools don’t exist yet, you build them. About the Role Restaurants are the heart of every neighborhood, yet most run on a patchwork of disconnected tools. We’re building DashOS, the operating system for the restaurant of the future. It’s one platform that connects delivery, in-store dining, reservations, and loyalty, across software, kiosk and POS hardware, and agentic experiences that take work off operators’ plates. As Principal Visual Designer, you’ll set the look, feel, and identity of DoorDash’s merchant products. You’ll own the visual direction for DashOS and give merchants a recognizable identity across every surface, including hardware, where no design conventions exist yet. These products already work. Your job is to make merchants love using them. Visual craft is the center of this role, and you’ll ship it yourself. You’ll prototype and use AI tools like Cursor and Claude to generate and refine UI, so your ideas reach production with full fidelity. You’ll also define the visual foundation of the design system (tokens, components, guidance, and examples) so designers, engineers, and AI tools all produce on-brand, high-quality UI. Engineering partners build and maintain the tooling, and you set the rules and the quality bar. You’ll report to the Senior Director, Product Design for Merchant. This role is hybrid, with 1–2 days a week in a Design Hub. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Set the visual direction for merchant products across DashOS and bring multiple teams around a shared vision, so the work compounds instead of duplicating. Ship high-craft interfaces with a clear point of view , turning complex, data-dense workflows into screens merchants can read at a glance in a busy kitchen or at the counter. Own the visual foundation of the design system : define the tokens, components, usage rules and examples that both people and AI tools apply. Review generated UI against that bar, record what good looks like, and improve the system based on how teams actually use it. Design for new surfaces. Create visual systems for points-of-sale, handhelds and agentic experiences where no existing paradigm applies. Influence through the work. Earn trust with prototypes and shipped products instead of decks, and keep your prototypes production-ready. Raise the bar across the team. Mentor senior designers, help close strong hires, and help people sharpen their sense of what to build and why. We’re excited about you because… You’ve designed interfaces that defined or reshaped a product’s look and feel, and your portfolio shows top-of-bar visual craft with range across brands and styles. You can build what you design. You work in React, TypeScript or similar, and use AI tools to explore directions and refine UI faster than you could by hand. You’ve set direction across a product area, and people adopted your work because it was good, not because you told them to. You’d rather build a visual system that makes 20 designers faster and more consistent than ship one great screen yourself. You’ve worked on complex, information-dense products such as point-of-sale, fintech, marketplaces or platform teams, and you’ve shipped with product and engineering partners, including pushing back constructively. Bonus: you’ve designed for devices or contexts with no existing design paradigm and built the visual system from scratch. jobs.descriptionText: RDQ427R613 About Databricks Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 10,000 organizations worldwide rely on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to unify and democratize data, analytics, and AI. As agents move from demos to real production work, Databricks is building the platform that lets enterprises create, govern, and collaborate with coding agents safely and at scale. Team & Product Omnigent is Databricks' platform for building, composing, governing, and sharing AI coding agents. It lets people create and coordinate agents across different model providers and execution environments - from the CLI and IDE to desktop, mobile, and managed enterprise surfaces. Users can watch agents work live, jump in to co-drive or fork a session, and package and share reusable agents. This is a rare chance to define and refine interaction patterns at enterprise scale: how people supervise fleets of agents, intervene at the right moment, understand risk, and build trust in autonomous work - starting with coding, review, and exploration workflows. The hard design problem isn't just showing what agents are doing; it's helping people know when to trust, when to step in, and how to recover when work goes off track - across a high-density desktop workspace and lightweight mobile moments. You'll design for two audiences at once: an open-source community shaping the future of agent workflows, and enterprise teams adopting agents in governed production. Role You'll be the IC design lead for how humans and fleets of agents work together on Omnigent - leading through product strategy, systems thinking, craft, and cross-functional collaboration. You're equally comfortable shipping small design changes directly in the codebase and prototyping your way through big, ambiguous problems that don't have a spec yet. You'll own the design direction across desktop and mobile, partner deeply with engineering and product, and translate the frontier of what agents can do into experiences that feel clear, controllable, trustworthy, and surprisingly effortless. What you'll do Own the desktop and mobile experience for live agent sessions end to end - from strategy and interaction models to visual polish and shipped detail. Shape the high-density orchestration workflows on desktop and the lightweight monitoring, review, approval, and intervention moments on mobile. Design directly in the codebase for well-scoped changes, working alongside engineers to ship real improvements rather than handing off static mocks. Use prototypes as a primary thinking tool. For large, vague problems, build interactive prototypes to explore, de-risk, and align the team on a direction. Invent the interaction language for agentic work: real-time multi-agent sessions, watch/co-drive/fork flows, human-in-the-loop approvals, agent status and transparency, error and recovery states, and trust. Define durable UX principles and interaction frameworks for agent collaboration, approvals, observability, and recovery that other teams reuse across Omnigent surfaces. Drive cross-platform consistency with a strong, scalable design system spanning desktop and mobile. Ground decisions in evidence - use research instincts and real usage to pressure-test ideas and know what to build next. What we're looking for A builder-designer who works fluently with AI tools. You can make small design changes directly in a codebase, and you use prototypes - and the agents themselves - to explore larger, ambiguous problems. You regularly use AI tools in your own design and build workflow. A portfolio of strong end-to-end craft - interaction design, visual/UI polish, and design-systems thinking - ideally on developer tools, AI/ML products, enterprise software, or other products for technical users. Staff-level scope and impact. A track record of shipping complex, high-quality developer products and leading design direction on hard problems. Self-directed, and comfortable in ambiguity - you help shape product direction when the path isn't defined. A strong collaborator who raises the level of high-quality critique, clear decision-making, and tight partnership with engineering and product. jobs.title: Staff Product Designer, AI
jobs.descriptionText: We’re looking for a Staff Product Designer who is excited to design the future of teamwork at the exact moment it is being reinvented. You’ll join Asana’s AI Design team to craft the experiences where AI does real work alongside people—from agents that take on tasks and AI-recommended workflows to the enterprise controls that build trust. Many of the interaction patterns we need don’t exist yet, giving you the opportunity to invent, ship, and scale them while setting the craft bar across our AI products and platform teams. We design the future of teamwork. Asana has a bold, ambitious mission: help humanity thrive by enabling the world’s teams to work together effortlessly. Our design team is at the heart of that mission. Asana Design is an inclusive and collaborative community made up of a diverse group of designers from different backgrounds (product, brand and content design, design operations, producers, motion design, film, copywriting). We love combining research, data insights, and peer feedback into a human-centered design process to produce designs that are core to the power of our applications. We partner with people across Asana to create our product, shape our brand, and drive greater impact through design—solving challenges, creating experiences that customers love, and taking the time to get weird and have fun along the way. We believe every designer should have the opportunity to grow and learn by utilizing their strengths and nurturing their interests. This role is based in our San Francisco office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. If you're interviewing for this role, your recruiter will share more about the in-office requirements. What you’ll achieve Lead the design of end-to-end experiences for Asana’s AI products, taking ambiguous, high-stakes problems from first framing to polished, shipped details. Define the interaction language for how people delegate to, steer, review, and trust AI in Asana—including how agents show their work, ask for input, explain their reasoning, recover from mistakes, and hand work back to people. Champion product excellence by raising the bar for interaction and visual craft so powerful AI capabilities feel clear, calm, and unmistakably Asana, while contributing AI-native patterns and components to our design system. Turn system and technical complexity into simple, dependable experiences by partnering with engineering and product to understand how models, tools, context, and permissions work, and designing for those realities. Treat AI as a design material by prototyping with real models, writing and refining prompts and instructions, and using real outputs and evaluations to shape what we ship. Build what you design using code-based prototypes to explore ideas and align partners, shipping changes to production alongside engineering when it is the fastest path. Design AI for multiplayer teams and enterprises by shaping the transparency, permissions, and admin controls that let organizations govern and roll out AI with confidence. Drive ideas across teams by connecting work across our AI products (such as AI Teammates, AI Studio, and Dash) and platform teams, bringing partners along with working prototypes, clear narratives, and a strong point of view—while elevating fellow designers through critique, pairing, and mentorship. About you 8+ years of experience in product design, with a track record of leading design on complex products at a senior level A portfolio showcasing interaction and visual design craft alongside a track record of shipping complex work at scale Real-world experience designing and shipping AI products—such as agents, assistants, AI-powered automation, or generative features—including designing for model behavior, uncertainty, and failure in partnership with engineering, research, and product teams Fluency with system and technical complexity, demonstrating the ability to reason about data models, permissions, integrations, and LLM constraints in behaviors and systems rather than just screens and flows Hands-on proficiency with modern AI tools, regularly prototyping with LLMs, iterating on prompts, and using AI-assisted design and coding tools in your everyday workflow Proven ability to lead work that spans multiple teams and drive alignment and execution without formal authority Customer-centric problem solver who gets close to users, uncovers unspoken needs, and uses research and data evidence to back design decisions At Asana, we're committed to building teams that include a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills, as this is critical to helping us achieve our mission. If you're interested in this role and don't meet every listed requirement, we still encourage you to apply. What we’ll offer Our comprehensive compensation package plays a big part in how we recognize you for the impact you have on our path to achieving our mission. We believe that compensation should be reflective of the value you create relative to the market value of your role. To ensure pay is fair and not impacted by biases, we're committed to looking at market value which is why we check ourselves and conduct a yearly pay equity audit. For this role, the estimated base salary range is between $223,000 - $253,000. The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. The listed range above is a guideline, and the base salary range for this role may be modified. In addition to base salary, your compensation package may include additional components such as equity, sales incentive pay (for most sales roles), and benefits. If you're interviewing for this role, speak with your recruiter to learn more about the total compensation and benefits for this role. We strive to provide equitable and competitive benefits packages that support our employees worldwide and include: Mental health, wellness & fitness benefits Career coaching & support Inclusive family building benefits Long-term savings or retirement plans In-office culinary options to cater to your dietary preferences These are just some of the benefits we offer, and benefits may vary based on role, country, and local regulations. If you're interviewing for this role, speak with your recruiter to learn more about the total compensation and benefits for this role. #LI-Hybrid #LI-HC1 About us Asana is a leading platform for human + AI collaboration. Millions of teams around the world rely on Asana to achieve their most important goals, faster. Asana has been named to Fortune's Best Workplaces for 7+ years and recognized by Fast Company, Forbes, and Gartner for excellence in workplace culture and innovation. jobs.descriptionText: About Pinterest: Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product. Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI. Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here . Pinterest is looking for a thoughtful, highly skilled Staff Motion Designer to join the Design Innovation team. You will define and evolve the motion design language that brings clarity, coherence, and delight to Pinterest across surfaces and flagship features. This is a hands-on, horizontal role for a rare blend of motion craft leader, systems thinker, and design technologist. You will establish reusable motion principles, patterns, tokens, and implementation guidance within the design system; partner directly with product and engineering teams to solve challenging interaction problems; and build tools and prototypes that make it easier to explore and ship exceptional motion at scale. Your impact will extend from the details of a single interaction to the cohesive experience of Pinterest as a whole. What you’ll do Define and evolve Pinterest’s motion design language – principles, interaction and transition patterns, timing and tokens, specifications, and guidance – so motion is intentional, coherent, accessible, and reusable across the product ecosystem. Lead motion direction for flagship and AI-forward experiences, using motion to clarify state, cause and effect, hierarchy, feedback, progress, and system responsiveness. Partner horizontally with product designers, engineers, product managers, researchers, and content designers to connect individual feature work to a shared motion strategy and raise the quality of shipped experiences. Turn high-craft explorations into scalable design system contributions that reduce ad hoc implementation, improve consistency, and enable teams to move faster with confidence. Rapidly prototype and validate motion ideas using the right medium – motion studies, design tools, code, AI-enabled tools, or custom prototypes – to create shared understanding and accelerate decisions. Work closely with engineering throughout implementation to solve technically ambitious animation challenges while balancing performance, platform conventions, accessibility, and maintainability. Develop or enable lightweight tools, templates, and workflows that help designers explore visual and motion ideas quickly and help engineering teams build sophisticated animations reliably. Stay at the leading edge of AI-enabled motion and visual-creation tools, applying them strategically to improve ideation, prototyping, and production while maintaining critical thinking, quality validation, and ownership of final outcomes. Conduct motion quality reviews, give actionable feedback on designs and implementations, and mentor designers in motion principles, systems thinking, prototype craft, and productive engineering partnership. Clearly articulate the rationale, tradeoffs, and user impact behind motion decisions to teams, leaders, and executives; build alignment around a high bar for motion craft and system quality. What we’re looking for Minimum 8 years of experience in motion design, product design, interaction design, or a closely related discipline, with a portfolio demonstrating exceptional motion craft in shipped digital products or platforms. Deep command of motion and interaction design principles, including timing, choreography, easing, spring behavior, feedback, and transitions – and strong judgment about when motion improves usability, comprehension, emotion, and trust. Strong product and systems thinking: able to connect craft decisions to user needs, product strategy, accessibility, implementation efficiency, and measurable impact. A collaborative, low-ego working style with a passion for learning, experimentation, mentoring, and inclusive design. jobs.title: Principal Product Designer - Consumer
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT US Our mission is to reinvent the way people learn, starting with language. Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages. Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana. ABOUT THE DESIGN TEAM We’re a small and mighty team of five that sit at the intersection of craft, research, invention and product thinking. We build consumer experiences used by millions, alongside B2B products that help organizations bring Speak to their teams. The design work is genuinely novel: inventing how someone talks to an AI tutor, what feedback feels like when you're learning out loud, how a roleplay session should land emotionally, and how you measure a true proficiency score. Our work shapes the future of how people learn with AI and we partner closely with Engineering, Learning Design, Product, and Analytics to do it. We stay close to our users and to how our experiences actually feel by prototyping with AI, testing conversation design and voice interaction, and getting comfortable with ambiguity. Our team takes craft seriously and has a lot of fun doing it. We developed our design principles in a multi-week offsite and iterate on them on a living board in our office. We take language classes together to ground our work in first principles. We stay close to our learners through team trips to Seoul, Tokyo, and Taipei, as well as lighter-touch interviews, surveys, betas, and AB tests. We believe in a critique and build culture with high trust, and also get a bit competitive over ping pong. We have something to prove: that learning products can be both deeply effective and beautifully crafted. If you want to do the most interesting design work of your career, let's talk. THE ROLE You’ll lead design for a major part of Speak’s consumer experience, either growth (activation, engagement, discovery) or core learning (AI tutoring, speaking practice, feedback, progression). We’ll pick the focus together based on your strengths. We don’t use seniority titles internally, but elsewhere this would be a Principal Product Designer: a hands-on IC who sets direction for a product area, drives our most consequential work, and helps other designers do their best work. - Set the experience vision for your area, grounded in empathy for learners across cultures and levels - Spot opportunities at the intersection of learner needs, product insights, and new AI capabilities, and make them tangible through prototypes that shape strategy with Product and Engineering - Invent interaction patterns for AI-powered learning that go beyond generic AI templates - Prototype and iterate quickly in AI tools, code, or interactive tools - Lead across team boundaries so the holistic experience feels cohesive - Use qualitative and quantitative signals to decide what to explore, ship, and improve WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR - Consumer design leadership. Likely 10+ years, including shaping a major consumer product area hands-on through shipping and iteration. Scope, craft, and impact matter more than years. - Close to users. You seek out real people, not just data, and test early with prototypes. - Product judgment. You frame the problem first and turn ambiguity into a clear vision others can build toward. - AI-native workflow. You use AI throughout your own workflow and build systems to unlock speed and quality in your creative and strategic work. - Taste and craft at speed. You have a point of view on great experiences and set the bar for the team. You also know when to stay scrappy vs when to spend time in polish. - Influence and mentorship. You build trust across teams, help groups reach decisions, and make other designers better. BONUS - Experience in language learning, education, or cross-cultural products - Contributions to design systems that scale beyond one team WHY WORK AT SPEAK 1. Join a fantastic, tight-knit team at the right time: we're growing very quickly, we've most recently raised our Series C from some of the top investors in the valley, and we've achieved product-market fit in our initial markets. You'd join at a magical time when a single person could significantly change the course of the company. 2. Do your life's work with people you’ll love working with: we care strongly about our craft and want every person at Speak to feel like they're growing every day. We believe in the idea that working with people you both enjoy and have respect for makes everything better. We hire thoughtfully and only work with people we admire deeply. 3. Global in nature: We're live in over 40 countries and launching in a number of new markets soon. We have dedicated offices in San Francisco, Ljubljana, Seoul, Tokyo, and Taipei, and you’ll have the opportunity to talk to users in each of these regions on a regular basis as well as travel. 4. Impact people's lives in a major way: Learning a language is one of the single most life-changing skills one can learn, and right now 99% of people never achieve their goal because the process is broken. We’re helping millions of people achieve their goals and improve their lives. jobs.descriptionText: Padlet https://padlet.com is building software for a good education. A good education is one that inspires curiosity, creativity, and community. Our software enables that through visual content creation and collaboration in millions of classrooms worldwide. There are some products that are so good, you feel delight using them. We aspire to build such products at Padlet, and are looking for a Senior Product Designer to help us fulfill our aspirations. This is an in-person role in San Francisco. You'll report directly to the CEO. RESPONSIBILITIES - Design of new products and features across mobile and web. - Coach less experienced designers in the design team. - Help hire more designers, if necessary. - Put Padlet in the hands of a billion people. QUALIFICATIONS - You like working hard. - You are honest. - You've designed beautiful software products. - Bonus: you have a good sense of humor. ABOUT PADLET - Vision: Every child in the world will grow up with Mickey Mouse and Padlet. - Product: We are making the default way of collecting and sharing thoughts on the Internet. People love the product. - Impact: We have 40 million users, making Padlet one of the most used apps on the planet. - Money: We are venture backed AND fiscally responsible. We are built to last one hundred years. - Badassery: We are only 60 odd people. That's over half a million active users per person. JOYS OF DESIGNING AT PADLET - We don't design with data or A/B tests unless we really don't know what the right answer is. - We ship. Your work will not be stuck in purgatory for years. - Your work will have a tremendous impact on global education. - Every artist craves an audience. You'll start with 40 million. - We value quality and craft. - We don't take ourselves too seriously. SORROWS OF DESIGNING AT PADLET - We don't design with data or A/B tests unless we really don't know what the right answer is. - CEO has very strong opinions about design and can often be incorrigible. - Work can be chaotic. "Change of plans. Let's do this instead." is not uncommon. - You will get hate mail whenever you redesign something. Many users feel very strongly about the product. SOME PEOPLE YOU‘D BE WORKING WITH - Collin Palmer: Exclusively listens to movie soundtracks when working, especially the Darth Vader theme. One man product machine from speccing to shipping. - Gerard Searchfield: Insists that wallabies and kangaroos are different animals, artificially inflating the biodiversity of his homeland. Will notice a 1px misalignment from 18 feet away. THE OFFICE - Our office https://padlet.link/sf-office-gmap is in the middle of Presidio, a beautiful national park. We’re a 5 minute walk from the beach. The WiFi works outdoors. jobs.title: Staff Conversational Designer
jobs.descriptionText: COMPANY OVERVIEW Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models. OPERATING PRINCIPLES Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together: 1. Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line. 2. Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools. 3. Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time. 4. Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet. We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team. AI-FIRST BY DEFAULT We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate. That means more than using the tools. We expect you to: - Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster. - Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you. - Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet. - Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place. We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment. Note: This is a remote role based in Pacific Time, with a preference for candidates located in San Francisco. ABOUT THE ROLE Deepgram builds the models and APIs that put voice agents into production at scale. What decides whether those agents feel human is not a screen. It is whether the agent knows when you have finished speaking, what it does when you cut it off, how it recovers from a misheard word, how it confirms something consequential before acting, and how it covers the milliseconds it cannot remove. Today those decisions live inside prompts and pipeline config, made ad hoc by whoever is closest to the problem. No one owns them end to end. We are hiring a Staff Conversational Designer to own them. You will define how Deepgram's voice agents converse: persona, turn-taking, repair, confirmation, and pacing. You will work directly with ML and Engineering on the tradeoffs that make those behaviors real, including endpointing, barge-in, and latency budgets. You will build the evals that tell us whether a conversation is actually good, and publish the guidance and reference experiences that show developers how to build natural conversations on the Voice Agent API. This is a leading edge role. Very few companies have a titled equivalent. You will be defining this discipline at Deepgram, not inheriting it. You'll report directly to the Director of Product Design. This is a Staff IC role, and your impact shows up mostly in the leverage you create for others: the patterns our own experiences run on, and the guidance our customers build against. Your first chapter: a documented persona and voice system, and turn-taking and repair behavior designed and shipped with Engineering. From there, scope expands into conversational-quality evals and developer-facing guidance. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Define the persona and voice system for Deepgram voice agents, and keep it coherent across experiences and use cases - Design turn-taking, barge-in, and end-of-turn behavior with ML and Engineering, tuning responsiveness against the risk of interrupting the user, per use case - Design conversational repair, no-match and no-input handling, and confirmation strategy, including guardrails that require confirmation before high-stakes actions - Own latency-aware pacing and perceived responsiveness: brevity, backchanneling, hold and filler speech, all against real-time budgets - Establish conversational-quality evals and a transcript review practice that turns production failures into a repeatable design loop - Build the reference agent experiences and developer-facing design guidance that demonstrate best-practice conversation on the Voice Agent API - Partner with ML and Research on ASR and TTS behavior, and on the quality criteria that define a good conversation - Set the conversation-design principles, review standards, and shared vocabulary the broader team adopts YOU’LL LOVE THIS ROLE IF YOU - Believe conversation is an interface with real craft behind it, not a prompt someone tunes on the side - Want the hard real-time problems: endpointing, barge-in, and the half-second you cannot design away - Get energized by being foundational, defining what good means for a discipline that does not exist here yet - Think the fastest way to raise quality is to make it measurable, then make it repeatable - Are excited by a category still inventing its interaction patterns, where the work is invention rather than iteration IT’S IMPORTANT TO US THAT YOU HAVE We care more about expertise and leadership than years of experience. - Deep experience designing conversational behavior for LLM-based voice agents or assistants, not only scripted IVR flows - Real fluency with the speech pipeline, from ASR through LLM to TTS, and a working understanding of where design decisions actually live inside it - A track record designing turn-taking, interruption, repair, and confirmation patterns that shipped and held up in production - Evidence of building quality measurement into the practice: evals, transcript review, benchmarks, or a structured failure-analysis loop - Exceptional writing craft, including sample dialogs, design guidance, and documentation that others can build against - Experience influencing engineering and ML partners on behavior they own, without authority over them - Experience designing for developers or technical users, including APIs, SDKs, and documentation surfaces - A working AI practice, with a point of view on where these tools help and where they mislead IT WOULD BE GREAT IF YOU HAD - Time on a named assistant or a production voice agent platform - Practice with Wizard of Oz testing and sample dialog methods - Hands-on work with eval tooling for LLM or voice quality - Experience in high-stakes or regulated conversation domains where confirmation and recovery carry real cost - Multilingual or cross-locale conversation design experience - Background in high-growth B2B companies with both self-serve and enterprise motions Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com http://deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT ABRIDGE Founded in 2018, Abridge is the first AI-native clinician intelligence platform organized around the patient, built for clinicians, and designed to help health systems coordinate the clinical, financial, and evidence-based decisions for every moment of care. Powered by purpose-built AI for healthcare, Abridge connects patients, providers, payers, and life sciences companies. This year, the platform will support more than 100 million patient-clinician conversations across more than 300 of the largest and most complex health systems in the U.S. With deep workflow integration, the Abridge clinician intelligence platform has been validated to support encounters in 28+ languages across specialties and care settings. Abridge is setting the industry standard for the responsible deployment of Al across health systems with continual and transparent Al evaluation. Clinical decision support references and cites gold-standard sources of evidence, and features like Linked Evidence map AI-generated documentation to source data, helping clinicians quickly trust and verify the output. Abridge was awarded Best in KLAS for Ambient AI in 2025 and 2026, in addition to other accolades, including TIME Best Inventions of 2024 and 2025, CNBC Disruptor 2025, and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies 2025. We are a growing team of practicing clinicians, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to transform healthcare. We have offices located in San Francisco, New York, and Pittsburgh. THE ROLE As a Product Designer at Abridge, you won’t just be designing software. You’ll be redesigning the future of healthcare delivery. You’ll create experiences that give clinicians back time, reduce cognitive load, and enable doctors to give their patients undivided attention again. Healthcare is broken in ways most people don’t see. Clinicians spend much of their time on administrative tasks, contributing to unprecedented burnout and compromised patient care. The current state of clinical documentation forces doctors to choose between looking at their patients and looking at their computers. We’re hiring product designers with a range of experience levels, strengths, and areas of expertise. Your scope will reflect what you bring to the team, but every designer at Abridge is expected to take meaningful ownership, navigate ambiguity, and help raise the quality of our products and practice. This role is for someone who dreams big and can reimagine experiences. You’ll work on problems that have never been solved before, in an industry where design decisions directly affect human lives and well-being. WHAT YOU’LL DO As a Product Designer, you’ll shape the product experience at Abridge, setting a high bar for taste, clarity, and strategic thinking across initiatives that directly impact clinicians, patients, and care teams. You’ll collaborate deeply with cross-functional partners, immerse yourself in the complexity of clinical workflows, and bring structure and empathy to ambiguous problems. Whether you’re exploring new ideas or refining existing experiences, you’ll advocate for design excellence throughout the product lifecycle. - Simplify the Complex: Tackle challenging and ambiguous design and customer problems, transforming complex clinical workflows and AI capabilities into intuitive, thoughtful, and delightful experiences. - Elevate Our Craft and Standards: Push the boundaries of visual and interaction design. Bring a strong command of design principles, motion, and prototyping; contribute to our evolving design standards; and ensure every detail and interaction is carefully considered. - Own End-to-End Design Execution: Design for today’s needs and tomorrow’s challenges, translating early ideas into clear product direction, high-fidelity designs, prototypes, and user flows. No task is too small or too large when it contributes to building an exceptional product. - Champion User-Centered Design: Advocate passionately for the clinicians and care teams who rely on our product every day. Engage in user research, synthesize insights, and ground design decisions in a deep understanding of users’ needs and pain points. - Lead Through Collaboration: Build strong partnerships across design, product, engineering, research, and other disciplines. Communicate clearly, invite feedback, and help teams make thoughtful decisions that balance user needs, business goals, and technical realities. WHAT YOU’LL BRING - 5+ years of experience shipping impactful digital products, ideally within complex domains. Experience with AI-powered products is a plus. - A strong track record of taking meaningful design initiatives from concept through launch and demonstrating an impact on users and the business. - The ability to bring clarity and momentum to ambiguous problems, adapting your approach and level of ownership to the needs of the work. - A high craft bar that you consistently meet and help others elevate. You care deeply about the details while maintaining sight of the larger product experience. - Exceptional communication, presentation, and storytelling skills, with the ability to articulate design rationale and influence partners across functions. - A highly collaborative spirit and low ego, along with a genuine desire to learn, teach, give and receive feedback, and grow with a fast-paced, high-performing team. BONUS POINTS IF YOU HAVE EXPERIENCE WITH - AI or machine-learning products - Consumer mobile products - Enterprise products We value people who are eager to learn new things and recognize that great team members might not perfectly match a job description. If you’re interested in the role but aren’t sure whether or not you’re a good fit, we’d still like to hear from you. Must be willing to work from our SF or NYC office at least 3x per week This position requires a commitment to a hybrid work model, with the expectation of coming into the office a minimum of (3) three times per week. Relocation assistance is available for candidates willing to move to San Francisco or New York. WHY WORK AT ABRIDGE? At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month. Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business. Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients. We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. jobs.title: Design Intern (Industrial / Mechanical)
jobs.descriptionText: MorphLabs · New York City · 5-month internship, on-site · Rolling applications About MorphLabs MorphLabs is building non-invasive telekinesis: a brain interface that turns movement intent into action, starting with people underserved by existing technology. We are starting with continuous, intuitive prosthetic control for upper-limb amputees, decoding movement intent from EEG in real time, without surgery or reliance on muscle sensors. We develop the hardware and models together, treating signal quality, learning and control as one problem. Prosthetics are where we start, not where we stop. We are a small, scrappy, high-throughput team in NYC. We have raised a substantial pre-seed round, with our seed round underway, and we move quickly between research and building. The role Our headset has to fit many different heads, hold electrodes in steady contact with the scalp, stay comfortable through a full day, and look like something a person would choose to wear in public. It also has to work alongside a prosthetic hand. Every one of those is a design problem, and each one affects the signal our models learn from. As a Design Intern, you'll spend five months on the physical design of that system, working directly with the founding team and our hardware engineers. You'll own a well-scoped project from first sketch to tested part, and be expected to ship something real: a headset revision we build, a fit or retention design we adopt, or a clear finding that changes what we try next. Most of the work is industrial design: fit, materials and mechanisms, plus a hand in how the headset looks and feels, carried all the way through mechanisms and working prototypes. Some of it is product and interface design for the software people use to set up, calibrate and control the system. This is not a side project. Interns work on the same hardware, participants and open problems as the rest of the team. What you'll do Form and identity. Work with the founders on how the headset looks, feels and wears: proportions, materials, color and finish, so it reads as something people choose to wear, not a lab instrument. Fit and comfort. Design for a wide range of head shapes and sizes, keep it comfortable through a full day, and make it fast to put on and adjust. Electrode retention. Design mechanisms that keep electrodes in stable contact with the scalp, and work with the hardware team to measure how each change affects signal quality. Miniaturization and enclosures. Work with our electrical engineers to package smaller boards and batteries into enclosures that are lighter, sturdier and easier to service. Prosthetic integration. Design the mounts, housings and interfaces that connect our system to prosthetic and robotic hands. Prototyping and testing. Move quickly from sketch to CAD to physical parts, test them on real people, and let each result shape the next iteration. Design for manufacture. Prepare parts for production runs and document designs so they can be built the same way every time. Product and interface design. Help design the setup, calibration and control screens that participants and users interact with, so the system is clear to use for people with and without limb differences. What you'll have Ownership. What you design goes into the headset we build and test, not a concept deck. Direct access to the founders. You'll work beside the people making the decisions, with no layers in between. Your designs on real heads, every day. We record new EEG daily, so your prototypes get worn and tested constantly. Our own hardware. We build our own headset, electrodes and amplifier, so no part of the system is off limits to redesign. An IRB already in place , covering both healthy participants and patients. The resources to do the work. Equipment and materials won't be the bottleneck. Who we're looking for We're hiring industrial designers who build: students, recent grads, or anyone whose portfolio shows physical products they designed and made themselves. We judge your work, not your school, degree or résumé. You don't need a background in neuroscience, BCI or prosthetics. What we expect: A portfolio of physical products you designed and built yourself, with a clear account of what was yours Form you can defend: the proportions, materials and finishes you chose, and why Sketch to CAD to physical prototype, many times over, with each round changing because of what you learned Design work that had to fit the human body for hours: wearables, medical devices, protective or sports gear Enough mechanical sense to make your designs actually work: tolerances, materials, mechanisms and assembly Testing with real people, and design changes you made because of what you saw Speed: iterations in days, not weeks What sets candidates apart: Experience with wearables, medical devices or consumer hardware Design for manufacturing experience, such as injection molding, machining or sheet metal Experience packaging electronics: enclosures, cable routing, battery and thermal constraints Product or interface design for software, especially for people with disabilities Experience with prosthetics, orthotics or assistive technology Work with soft goods, textiles or flexible materials The bar is high on purpose. If your portfolio clears it, apply, whatever your background. Logistics and Compensation Duration: 5 months, full-time Location: Onsite, New York City Compensation: $6500/Mo Start Date(s): December 1st or January 5th Rolling applications
