jobs.title: Senior Graphic Designer, Brand Campaigns
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT SUNO We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world. Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible. Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA). ABOUT THE ROLE We’re seeking a highly creative, multidisciplinary Senior Graphic Designer to join Suno’s Brand & Creative Team. You’ll work across brand, culture, and product—helping translate Suno’s creative vision into expressive, high-impact design across platforms and formats. This role plays a key part in evolving Suno’s brand across marketing campaigns, artist partnerships, in-product brand moments, and culture-defining activations. You’ll help shape how Suno shows up visually at moments that matter—from product launches and campaigns to artist collaborations and creative brand expressions. In this role, you’ll partner closely with creative leadership, designers, writers, motion artists, project managers, product designers, and cross-functional teams to concept, design, and execute work that evolves Suno’s brand. This role is ideal for a designer who delivers innovative, standout work with precision—evolving the brand through bold ideas that are executed confidently and consistently within Suno’s creative direction. Check out the Suno version of this role here! https://suno.com/s/p71hcfuWMLRPqgt8 WHAT YOU’LL DO - Design and execute multidisciplinary creative work that evolves Suno’s brand across campaigns, artist partnerships, in-product moments, and brand activations. - Create innovative, high-impact design while maintaining precision and consistency within Suno’s creative direction and brand guidelines. - Support artist collaborations and partnerships, developing visuals and assets that authentically reflect both the artist’s voice and Suno’s identity. - Contribute to product launches and in-product brand moments, partnering with the Design Director and cross-functional teams (product design, GTM, Growth) to ensure a cohesive visual experience. - Translate ideas into polished, production-ready assets across digital, social, print, and motion formats. - Iterate quickly and thoughtfully in a fast-paced, collaborative environment, embracing feedback to evolve ideas and elevate the work. - Design with a global audience and end-to-end user experience in mind. - Maintain a high bar for craft and attention to detail across every execution. - Collaborate closely with designers, writers, motion artists, and cross-functional partners to bring great work to life. - Use AI and emerging creative tools as a core part of the creative and systems workflow, bringing hands-on experience with AI tooling to develop new creative approaches, accelerate production and build scalable, repeatable systems. WHAT YOU’LL NEED - 8+ years of experience as a graphic designer working across multiple disciplines (brand, marketing, digital, social, campaigns, content, etc.). - A strong portfolio showcasing innovative thinking and executional excellence across a range of formats and platforms. - A multidisciplinary designer. You have experience working across brand, marketing, campaigns, content, and digital surfaces, and you adapt your craft fluidly across formats. Motion experience is a strong bonus. - Craft-obsessed. You can zoom out to see the big picture and zoom all the way in to the smallest details—from typography and layout to motion, spacing, and final polish. You know great work is built through care, precision, and attention to detail. - Collaborative to your core. You love working closely with designers, motion artists, writers, product teams, and partners—embracing feedback and shaping ideas together to create work that’s both inspiring and practical. - A proactive builder. You thrive in ambiguity, spot opportunities early, and bring structure to creative chaos—proposing ideas, improving systems, and pushing work forward. - Comfortable in a fast-paced environment. You can juggle multiple projects, iterate quickly and thoughtfully, and maintain a high bar for quality under changing timelines. - Brand-forward and user-aware. You think globally, care about the end-to-end user experience, and design with both consistency and cultural relevance in mind. - Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite and Figma; motion design skills (After Effects, animated prototypes, etc.) are a strong bonus. - Passionate about music and culture. You’re excited by artists, creative expression, and emerging technology—and motivated by shaping how people experience music. - Fluent in AI tooling and systems. You understand how to integrate emerging AI tools into design and system workflows, using them to expand creative possibilities, accelerate production and build repeatable systems. ADDITIONAL NOTES: - Applicants must be eligible to work in the US. - This is an in-person role working at our NYC offices. PERKS & BENEFITS - Company Equity Package - 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k) - Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options) - 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time - 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave - Creative Education Stipend - Generous Commuter Allowance - In-Office Lunch (5 days per week) COMPENSATION The annual salary range for this role is $150-175K + target equity + benefits (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k) Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Procure to Pay
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT ZIP Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement — built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before. The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA. Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups. ABOUT THE TEAM Product Design at Zip is a tight-knit team that cares deeply about craft, collaboration, and building consumer-grade experiences for complex enterprise workflows. Designers are strategic partners to Product and Engineering in their product area: they run their own research with direct access to customers, shape scope, and see their work through to launch. We build on Birch, our design system, and we use AI across how we design and build. Procure-to-Pay (P2P) spans a wide scope:: purchase orders, invoices, and payments, and the workflows that keep enterprise spend committed and accurate. It is also where Zip's next five years take shape: we believe every dollar of enterprise spend can be orchestrated, automated, and optimized by Zip, and P2P is where those dollars are committed and paid. You'll join an established team with a dedicated PM, a strong engineering group, and direct lines to the customers you're designing for. You'll work in a highly collaborative environment with designers, engineers, and product managers who care deeply about craft and are obsessed with delivering a great experience for our customers. WHAT YOU'LL DO As a Senior Product Designer on P2P, you'll own product design for one of its core areas and design this surface's first AI agents: purchase orders that maintain themselves, transactions that code and reconcile themselves, and the groundwork for spend that optimizes itself. RESPONSIBILITIES - Learn the domain: Build a deep understanding of P2P and of the finance and procurement teams who run on it, so your design decisions hold up. - Own the work from problem to launch: Frame the problem, shape the scope with your PM, and own end-to-end experiences at the core of P2P: creation and approval workflows, change management, alerts, and the dashboards enterprises run their spend on. Stay with it through launch and polish. - Get in front of customers: Run your own research through with our bench of beta customers, and test your work with the AP teams and requesters who live in these flows. - Prototype with AI, decide with engineers: Use Claude, Figma Make, Cursor, or whatever gets an idea clickable fastest, and partner closely with your PM and engineers to brainstorm, define, and decide what ships. - Design the hard states and hide the complexity: Design full transaction lifecycles, including all the edge cases, where user trust is won or lost, and keep the default experience simple. - Shape our first agents: Design agent experiences grounded in structured procurement data: automation that users can verify and trust. - Raise the team's craft: Share work early in regular design reviews with the broader design team, and share what you learn along the way. QUALIFICATIONS - 5+ years of experience designing complex B2B or workflow products; procurement, payments, or fintech experience is a plus. - Strong visual and interaction craft: your shipped work shows excellent execution and attention to detail, without sacrificing usability. - Experience shipping at least one full product or significant feature end to end as the lead designer. - Experience running your own research: finding the right customers, asking the right questions, and turning what you hear into design decisions. - Experience iterating closely with engineers on both UX and visual design to get the details just right. - A point of view: you can defend design decisions with PMs and engineers, and change your mind when the evidence says you should. - You embrace AI in what you build and in how you work: you design AI-assisted workflows users can verify and trust, and you prototype with Claude, Figma Make, Cursor, or whatever gets your ideas into something clickable fastest. - Fluency in Figma and prototyping tools. - Understanding of the technical constraints of building web applications. NICE TO HAVES - You've shipped AI experiences, such as agents or assistants that act on a user's behalf, and designed the moments that make them trustworthy: showing what the AI did and why, where a human reviews or approves, and how to correct it when it's wrong. - Experience contributing to a team's product vision, and the desire to keep doing it: you can show where the product should go, not only the next release. - You're excited to be a culture carrier and help shape our growing Toronto office with the other designers there. The salary range for this role is $165,000-$190,000 CAD. The salary for this position is determined based on a variety of job-related factors that may include location, relevant experience, education, or particular skills and expertise. This posting is for a current vacancy. As part of our hiring process, Zip uses AI-enabled tools to assist in screening and assessing candidates, including resume review and interview documentation. All hiring decisions are made by people. PERKS & BENEFITS At Zip, we’re committed to providing our employees with everything they need to do their best work. - 📈 Start-up equity - 🦷 Health, vision & dental coverage options - 🍽️ Catered breakfast, lunch, & dinner - 🌴 Flexible PTO - 🏋️‍♀️ ClassPass membership - 🚍 Monthly commuter benefit - 🚠 Team building events & happy hours - 💻 Home office stipend - 🛜 Phone/internet reimbursement - 🍼 Paid parental leave - 🤖 AI token usage We're looking to hire Zipsters and that means hiring people who take ownership, communicate openly, have an underdog mindset, and are excited to increase the pace of innovation for every business in the world. We encourage all candidates to apply even if your experience doesn't exactly match up to our job description. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workspace where everyone (regardless of age, religion, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, and more) feels like they belong. We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.title: Staff/Principal Design Systems Lead
jobs.descriptionText: At Render, we’re building the modern cloud platform for developers creating AI-native, full-stack, multi-service applications. Our mission is to eliminate the tradeoff between the power of hyperscalers and the simplicity of developer-friendly platforms—so teams can ship fast, scale reliably, and focus on their product, not infrastructure. Unlike complex hyperscalers or ephemeral edge/serverless solutions, Render offers a developer-first experience with persistent compute, dynamic autoscaling, built-in orchestration, and observability, allowing teams to launch, scale, and manage real-world applications without writing infrastructure code or managing servers. Whether you're building LLM-powered applications, scalable SaaS products, or async processing pipelines, Render empowers teams to move fast and scale confidently from MVP to millions of users. Our platform is trusted by over 7 million developers worldwide and continues to grow rapidly. In February 2026, we raised an additional $100M in Series C financing, bringing our total funding to $260M, to accelerate our vision of making cloud infrastructure both powerful and intuitive—designed for the speed of modern AI development. We’re a diverse and talented team that values craft, velocity, and user experience. If you’re excited to help shape the future of the intelligent cloud and empower developers everywhere, we’d love to hear from you. APPLYING TO RENDER We're seeking candidates who possess high integrity, humility, and an insatiable drive to learn. Through reasoned discussions and continuous feedback, we strive to improve both individually and collectively. We foster an environment of mutual trust and respect, empowering effective debate to achieve the best outcomes for our customers and team. We especially encourage members of underrepresented groups in the tech community to apply and understand that not all successful candidates will meet each requirement listed. Our interview process is unique to each role, and we value the candidate experience just as much as our customer experience. We hope your conversations with us reflect a thoughtful process that is illuminative, enjoyable, and respectful of your time. ABOUT THE ROLE How we build software is changing. Designers are prototyping in code, engineers are shipping polished interfaces, and agents are starting to build directly into the product. More people and more things can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less. We're looking for a Staff/Principal Founding Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into Render's foundations. This isn't about maintaining a component library. It's about enabling designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Render, without a designer making every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change. At a company whose whole promise is a platform that just works, the design system is how we keep craft scaling as the product and the team grows. This role starts hands-on. You're a designer first, with the technical depth to get into the code. You'll partner with the Head of Design to set the vision, then do the foundational work yourself: decide where or whether our Figma library lives and how it operates, get deep into what an AI-ready design system really means, and prototype, test, and ship the system in code. As the function grows, you'll build and lead the team around it. You're energized by building from the ground up, not inheriting something finished. Here's what makes this role urgent and specific to us: our users are developers, and they're increasingly building with AI agents. That cuts both ways. Inside Render, teams reach for an agent before they check the docs — so a system that isn't legible to AI quietly gets bypassed, and quality drifts toward generic output. And externally, we're building the platform where developers deploy AI-native apps and agents. The person in this role treats the design system as infrastructure for humans, machines, and velocity and has a point of view on what that takes: machine-readable documentation, system rules exposed where agents can read them, an architecture that keeps the brand and accessibility layers ours, and evaluations that catch drift before it ships. This role reports to the Head of Design. THIS ROLE IS FOR YOU IF YOU'RE EXCITED BY: Making great design reproducible, by people and agents. Raise the quality of Render's product and encode what makes it good, so a designer, an engineer, or an agent can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same. Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition rules, interaction patterns, agent-readable guidance, and evaluations, so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality. Building and leading a team that multiplies everyone else's impact. Start hands-on, then create the direction, ambitious goals, and caring-but-demanding environment that let a team do the best work of their careers. The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Render, human or agent, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Set the system's vision and direction. Decide what to preserve, evolve, simplify, or replace based on what builders and customers need — and turn that into focused work, much of which you'll do yourself at first. - Build the foundations hands-on. Early on, you are the team: setting the architecture, shipping the components, writing the guidance, and establishing the quality bar through your own work before there's anyone to delegate to. - Build and lead the team that owns the system. As the function grows, hire and develop it — set priorities and ownership, give direct feedback, hold a high bar, and help people do the best work of their careers. - Elevate Render's visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility — and the states beyond the happy path, which is where developer tools earn their reputation. - Make the system legible to AI, not just humans. Lead the work to make Render's design system AI-ready: machine-readable documentation, system rules and tokens exposed where agents can reach them (e.g. via MCP), and an architecture that shrinks the context an agent needs while keeping the brand and accessibility layers ours. The goal: agents building on Render produce on-brand, compliant work by default. - Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use — layered and headless where that scales better than rigid bundles. - Define and measure quality, including AI output. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks — testing generated output against the system's standard, not just whether people use the tools. - Earn adoption. Work alongside product teams, teach through examples, and turn recurring questions and exceptions into improvements. A system lives or dies on whether people, and their agents, reach for it. - Keep moving as the ground shifts. Experiment as models and tools evolve, share what you learn, and change direction when the evidence calls for it. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - A track record of setting direction and delivering outcomes in design systems or design engineering — and the appetite to build a function from the ground up before leading a team. You create clarity in ambiguity, make decisions, give difficult feedback, and keep momentum without dropping the quality bar. Experience leading or developing designers/design engineers is a strong plus, as this role grows in that area. - Exceptional visual and interaction design skills. Your work shows a clear point of view, detail that borders on obsessive, and an ability to make complex experiences feel simple — the kind of craft other practitioners admire. - Deep systems thinking, and experience building systems other teams actually adopt. You can show how your work improved both their speed and the quality of what shipped — not just that it existed. - Strong technical fluency. You can prototype and build in code, understand front-end architecture (component API design, tokens, theming, layered/headless patterns), and work through implementation tradeoffs with engineers — not just hand off specs. - Hands-on use of AI in your work, and a real point of view on AI-ready design systems. You understand where AI helps and where it fails, how to improve its output rather than accept it, and what it takes for a system to serve machines as well as humans. You don't need to have shipped all of it, but you should be able to say where you'd start and why. - Strong product judgment and developer empathy. You stay close to the people who use what you build and connect system decisions to real workflows and outcomes. Fluency with developers and technical products is a strong plus — our users are engineers, and the system has to serve them and the agents they build with. NICE-TO-HAVES - Experience building developer tools, cloud platforms, or infrastructure products where UX is a competitive advantage. - Hands-on experience making a design system AI-ready: machine-readable documentation, MCP or similar agent access, layered/headless architecture, or evaluation frameworks for AI-generated output. - Experience building developer or designer tools that became part of other teams' daily workflow. - Experience leading a major design-system migration or a company-wide change in how teams build. - Experience evolving a system across platforms, or connecting product and brand experiences. - Founder or early-stage startup experience. If this role excites you but you don’t meet every single requirement, we’d still love to hear from you—your unique experience might be just what we need. BENEFITS - 4 weeks of paid vacation. - 14 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all parents to bond with a newly born, adopted, or fostered child. We will also work with you to create a supportive plan of return. - Long-term disability, life insurance, and 401K plans. - 100% employer-paid medical coverage and 99% employer-paid dental and vision coverage for you and a dependent. FSAs and HSAs are available as well. - Monthly lifestyle stipend for wellness, mental health and therapy, hobbies, etc. - Monthly cell phone and internet subsidy. - Commuter benefits for Renders in the Bay Area, and home office stipends for remote Renders. - Continuous learning benefits & related support. This position is generally not eligible for new visa sponsorship. At Render's discretion, the business may sponsor existing visa transfers. Applicants who require sponsorship must receive business authorization. Render is an equal-opportunity employer. We know that employing a team rich in diverse thoughts, experiences, and opinions allows our employees, product, and community to flourish. We make all employment decisions including hiring, evaluation, termination, promotional, and training opportunities, without regard to race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, physical handicap, mental disability, medical condition, disability, gender or identity or expression, pregnancy or pregnancy-related condition, marital status, height and/or weight. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. We encourage all who are interested to apply. We can't wait to hear from you! jobs.title: Senior Design Systems Engineer
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a Design Systems Engineer to be one of the few engineers building the components that every Ramp product team uses — the person who makes our design system real in code. You’ll work in close partnership with our design systems lead and designers: they decide what the rules are, and you decide how to enforce them. Sometimes that’s a component that won’t allow a bad pattern. Sometimes it’s a codebase move that makes the right path the easy one. Sometimes it’s automation that catches drift before it spreads. With AI agents now writing much of the UI, this role is also at the frontier of a changing craft. You’ll help decide what the system has to guarantee when humans and agents are both building on top of it — because agents don’t settle for the happy path, and the system needs to hold up either way. Having worked as a designer (or deeply alongside one), you understand the design-eng collaboration challenges firsthand. You’re driven to improve it because you’ve lived with the pain points. You excel in UI and accessible design, prefer working directly in-browser, and get excited about emerging CSS properties. This is an IC role on a small team, which means you’ll have real say in architecture, API design, and the tradeoffs that shape how Ramp builds — foundational, detail-obsessed frontend work with an outsized impact on every screen we ship. What You’ll Do - Build and evolve the components and APIs that every product team at Ramp depends on - Make the enforcement call: when to encode a rule in the component itself, when to leave it to guidance, and when to invest in automation that catches drift - Partner with our design systems lead and designers to turn UX patterns and principles into working, consistent components - Shape the system so it holds up when both engineers and AI agents are building on it - Contribute to internal tooling and infrastructure that keeps velocity high without sacrificing quality - Champion the user experience and accessibility of our products, and keep the quality bar high - Help designers and engineers across Ramp ship faster with elegant, consistent component APIs and a focus on developer experience - Advocate for users by continuously iterating on our core products and experiences - Participate in day-to-day team rituals like design crit, story creation, and weekly stand-ups - Help us hire and grow the team to bring more craft and more perspectives to the work What You Need - Tech/startup or digital product agency experience, or equivalent - A strong frontend engineer who could pass any engineering loop at Ramp — real hands-on skill, not just prompting AI to write code - Experience building design system components and APIs, not only consuming them - Excellent front-end development skills in semantic HTML, CSS (up to date on latest features) and JavaScript (and frameworks, pref. jobs.title: Senior / Staff Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires. Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 50,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship. Quality is our competitive advantage. Every member of our fully remote team is a maker at heart, caring deeply about the quality and feel of our work. While the industry optimizes for speed and metrics alone, we believe that craft and quality have lasting value. Quality creates gravity — it pulls people toward our team and product rather than requiring us to push. This philosophy drives everything we do, from product decisions to hiring choices. For this role, we expect robust design skills, sharp product thinking, and the ability to engage in technical discussions. We work in small, autonomous project teams, where engineers are paired tightly with designers to explore ideas, build prototypes, deploy internal builds, and ultimately ship to customers. You will be a key element of projects from beginning to end. Location & work mode Linear is a remote-first company, with optional co-working offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. This role is open to candidates based in North America. You can work from anywhere within this region. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel. What you'll do - Pair closely with engineering and product to initiate and complete roadmap projects, no hand-offs - Spot opportunities to redesign or refine key screens and flows, as well as smaller quality issues and “paper cuts” as you use Linear - Create mockups, prototypes, and high-fidelity visuals to communicate ideas and describe their execution - Guide and inspire fellow designers through collaborative critique of work-in-progress - Use and improve our lightweight design system components - Help with hiring new teammates that can elevate our team and product What we’re looking for - 7+ years experience designing software - Courage to ask questions, experiment, and advocate for what you feel is right - Humility to accept feedback, adapt your thinking, and iterate toward the best solution - Experience with prototyping in Figma (and beyond with tools like AI, HTML/CSS, Origami) - Ability to distill problems and feedback, then design clear, focused solutions - Effective written and verbal communication skills — much of our work is async What we offer We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with. jobs.title: Principal Designer, Design Systems
jobs.descriptionText: Ibotta is seeking a Principal Designer, Design Systems to join our innovative team and contribute to our mission to Make Every Purchase Rewarding. You will build a design system that lets designers, engineers, and AI agents produce consistent, high-quality product experiences by default. We are looking for a lead designer to set its direction and design it, working alongside the design team and engineering to build it in code. The system exists today as a Figma library approaching parity with our products, and is meant to grow into a shared foundation across everything Ibotta builds. The goal is to raise the quality floor without slowing teams down, leaving designers more room to craft the experiences that matter most. Ibotta has a suite of software tools that touch multiple surfaces and users. As we continue to grow and scale our products we need a design system that scales with them and allows for both human and AI agent workflows to use the system. This position is located in Denver, Colorado as a hybrid position requiring 3 days in office (Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday). Candidates must live in the United States. Not based in Denver? We will offer a relocation bonus to help make your move to the Mile High City a smooth one. What you will be doing: - Own the system's direction. Decide what to keep, change, or retire based on what builders and customers need, and hold the line on craft as the system grows. Own the roadmap, contribution model, versioning, release process, and documentation. - Design the foundations and components, covering the states beyond the happy path (empty, loading, error), with accessibility and motion built in from the start - Define the governance model for how components are proposed, reviewed, accepted, and deprecated. - Partner with the design team and with engineering so the system lives in code, not only in design files. Design nuance lives in the code as much as in the visuals, so stay close to both without owning the implementation. - Earn adoption. Help product teams move onto the system, teach through examples, and keep releases predictable with clear versioning, deprecation paths, and notice before breaking changes. - Define and measure quality. Set up repeatable evaluations on real tasks to see whether builders ship better work faster, with less rework. Work with content design so the system carries language as well as components. - Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference examples, and guidance that let designers, product managers, engineers, and AI agents build products that align to a single design language. - Lead research with the people who use the system. Talk to internal designers, engineers, and PMs, watch how they build, and turn recurring questions and workarounds into improvements. - Embrace and uphold Ibotta's Core Values: Integrity, Boldness, Ownership, Teamwork, Transparency, and A Good Idea Can Come from Anywhere What we are looking for: - 10+ years of design experience, including owning a design system at a company with more than one product surface - Bachelor's degree in Design, HCI, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience - Evidence of adoption, not just creation. We want to hear how you got teams to use what you built - Deep Figma skills, including variables, component architecture, and library management at scale - Working fluency with front-end code, enough to partner credibly on implementation and to judge whether what shipped matches what was designed - Familiarity with collaboration and documentation tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence) and AI tooling - Experience defining governance and contribution models that survive without constant enforcement - Comfort owning a capability outright, setting direction rather than waiting for it, and partnering with designers, researchers and product managers on roadmaps. About Ibotta ("I bought a...") Ibotta (NYSE: IBTA) is a leading performance marketing platform allowing brands to deliver digital promotions to over 200 million consumers through a network of publishers called the Ibotta Performance Network (IPN). The IPN allows marketers to influence what people buy, and where and how often they shop – all while paying only when their campaigns directly result in a sale. American shoppers have earned over $2.6 billion through the IPN since 2012. The largest tech IPO in history to come out of Colorado, Ibotta is headquartered in Denver, and is continually listed as a top place to work by The Denver Post and Inc. Magazine. To learn more about what our Tech teams are doing day to day, visit Building Ibotta on https://medium.com/building-ibottaMedium.com http://Medium.com Additional Details: - This position is located in Denver, CO, and includes competitive pay, flexible time off, benefits package (including medical, dental, vision), Employee Stock Purchase Program, and 401k match. Denver office perks include paid parking, snacks, and occasional meals. - Base compensation range: $185,000 - $205,000 Equity is included in the overall compensation package. This compensation range is specific to the United States labor market and may be adjusted based on actual experience. - Ibotta is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Ibotta's employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected status. - Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. - Applicants are accepted until the position is filled. - For the security of our employees and the business, all employees are responsible for the secure handling of data in accordance with our security policies, identifying and reporting phishing attempts, as well as reporting security incidents to the proper channels. jobs.title: Staff Web Designer
jobs.descriptionText: From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven. About Us Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data. Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on. Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions. As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact. During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites. About the Role Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies. We're looking for a strategic, hands-on Staff who loves solving complex UX challenges, building scalable systems, and turning ideas into real experiences. This role is ideal for a scrappy, systems-minded designer who thrives on ownership, enjoys getting into the details, and is excited to be the primary designer shaping Fivetran's web experiences. You will own the design strategy and hands-on execution for fivetran.com and getdbt.com, building scalable design systems that balance consistency with flexibility. You'll choose when to use existing patterns, when to evolve them, and when a unique experience calls for something new. To bring your projects to life, you will partner closely with Web Strategy, Web Engineering, Brand, Growth Marketing, Product Marketing, and Product teams. Success in this role requires balancing big-picture systems thinking with a willingness to roll up your sleeves. You should be comfortable moving between strategy, wireframes, prototypes, and design systems, making thoughtful trade-offs to ship high-quality work quickly. You will champion AI-powered tools and new ways of working, create scalable processes that reduce repetitive work, and help shape how web design operates as the business grows. We're looking for someone resourceful, opinionated, curious, and energized by building and thinking in systems. You will build the foundations that make great web experiences easier to create, evolve, and scale. This is a full-time hybrid position based out of our Oakland, Denver, Austin, New York or Philadelphia office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration, including two days in the office each week to connect and build as a team. Technologies You’ll Use Figma Webflow Sanity Claude Codex Jira Google Analytics (GA4) Amplitude Microsoft Clarity What You’ll Do Own the end-to-end design strategy and execution for Fivetran and dbt, translating complex web strategy into scalable design systems from concept through launch. Operate as the sole web designer, independently driving high-impact initiatives with a scrappy, pragmatic mindset that balances speed, quality, and technical feasibility. Shape and evolve the design systems that power our website, including reusable components, design standards, and interaction patterns that improve consistency and accelerate time to market. Lead AI innovation for web design, experimenting with emerging tools and building repeatable workflows that accelerate prototyping, production, and implementation. Partner closely with web strategy to connect designs to business outcomes and with web engineering to translate designs into real experiences. jobs.title: Senior Product Designer - Click UI
jobs.descriptionText: ClickHouse is one of the fastest-growing databases in the world, and our design team is at an inflection point. As we expand into new solution areas, we’re looking for a designer who codes. You’ll own the design side of Click UI, ClickHouse’s open source design system. As a member of a solution-oriented product team, you’ll see those system-level design decisions through to end users. jobs.title: Staff Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: At Render, we’re building the modern cloud platform for developers creating AI-native, full-stack, multi-service applications. Our mission is to eliminate the tradeoff between the power of hyperscalers and the simplicity of developer-friendly platforms—so teams can ship fast, scale reliably, and focus on their product, not infrastructure. Unlike complex hyperscalers or ephemeral edge/serverless solutions, Render offers a developer-first experience with persistent compute, dynamic autoscaling, built-in orchestration, and observability, allowing teams to launch, scale, and manage real-world applications without writing infrastructure code or managing servers. Whether you're building LLM-powered applications, scalable SaaS products, or async processing pipelines, Render empowers teams to move fast and scale confidently from MVP to millions of users. Our platform is trusted by over 7 million developers worldwide and continues to grow rapidly. In February 2026, we raised an additional $100M in Series C financing, bringing our total funding to $260M, to accelerate our vision of making cloud infrastructure both powerful and intuitive—designed for the speed of modern AI development. We’re a diverse and talented team that values craft, velocity, and user experience. If you’re excited to help shape the future of the intelligent cloud and empower developers everywhere, we’d love to hear from you. APPLYING TO RENDER We're seeking candidates who possess high integrity, humility, and an insatiable drive to learn. Through reasoned discussions and continuous feedback, we strive to improve both individually and collectively. We foster an environment of mutual trust and respect, empowering effective debate to achieve the best outcomes for our customers and team. We especially encourage members of underrepresented groups in the tech community to apply and understand that not all successful candidates will meet each requirement listed. Our interview process is unique to each role, and we value the candidate experience just as much as our customer experience. We hope your conversations with us reflect a thoughtful process that is illuminative, enjoyable, and respectful of your time. ABOUT THE ROLE Render’s mission is simple: eliminate the tedious work of building software by providing a cloud platform that just works. We’re evolving from the go-to platform for solo developers into the backbone for fast-scaling teams. As our users’ apps grow from a single service into complex, multi-service architectures, our biggest challenge is keeping it all feeling simple. We need a Product Designer to take that "pile of parts" and turn it into a cohesive system that actually makes sense. As a Staff IC, you'll also help raise the bar across the organization through mentorship, design leadership, and thoughtful cross-functional influence. This is a craft-focused IC role, and it's web UI at its most demanding. You'll own the surfaces developers depend on when the clock is ticking and things are breaking. Designing for infrastructure is unique: your screens see the most traffic when the user is most stressed, and "failure" is a first-class state, not an edge case. We’re looking for someone who finds that responsibility energizing. You’ll join a design team that takes its craft seriously, with weekly critiques and deep cross-functional collaboration. You’ll thrive here if you love untangling complex, messy problems and turning them into accessible, beautiful experiences. YOU WILL: - Make a multi-service system legible at a glance. Design the views that let a developer see how their services connect and depend on each other, instead of stitching the picture together one service at a time. This comprehension gap is where design can make a complicated system feel cohesive and friendly. - Design system-level observability. Aggregated logs, metrics, deploys, and events across a whole project, filterable by environment and resource — so a developer can answer "what's going on with my system" in one place. This is high-density information design where hierarchy, scanning speed, and progressive disclosure are the whole game. - Design deployment as a coordinated act. When an application has many services, coordination gets hard. You'll design cross-service deployment and rollback, and a preview model so shipping feels safe at any scale. - Design and consider all product states. You'll own the "unglamorous" moments. Like build errors, failed deploys, and empty states, and turn them into helpful experiences. Since developer tools earn their reputation by how they handle problems, your focus is on guiding the user to success even when things go wrong. - Own a first-run experience worth recommending. The path from signup to first successful deploy is where trust starts. You'll design it so that a developer's first ten minutes make them want to tell someone. - Contribute to where the platform goes next. Alongside the shipping work, you'll bring concept explorations and a strong point of view to a design-led discovery track, shaping the platform's future through a weekly critique cadence with the rest of the team. WE'RE LOOKING FOR: - 7+ years of relevant experience. Whether you’ve worked on developer tools, cloud infrastructure, or another complex, high-stakes product, we care more about your impact than your title. - Exceptional taste and craft. You have an eye for detail that borders on obsessive — typography, spacing, motion, density, interaction feedback. You notice when something is 2px off and it bothers you, and you've shipped work other practitioners admire. - Strong information architecture. You can take a tangle of objects and relationships and make it feel like one obvious thing. - You design the whole journey, not a screen at a time. Your portfolio shows a user carried coherently across every surface a feature touches — entry point to empty state to failure to recovery — not a set of polished screens that don't add up to a system. - Fluent in developer language. You know your way around services, CI/CD, and deployments. You don’t need to have built a cloud platform before, but you’re curious enough to get deep into the weeds of how it works. - Respect for failure states. You believe an error message is an interface, and you design for the user having a bad day, not just the happy path. - Systems fluency. You're comfortable working in and contributing to a design system as the product's surface area grows, extending it rather than fighting it. - Strong product judgment under fast launch velocity. You frame problems well, prioritize ruthlessly, and know which details matter and which can wait. - Clear, direct communication and a genuinely collaborative way of working with product and engineering partners — including sharing a problem space with another designer without needing hard fences between you. NICE-TO-HAVES: - Experience designing complex dashboards, monitoring tools, or console interfaces where data density and high-stakes clarity matter. - You've been on-call, run side projects, or debugged systems in production. You don’t just design for developers; you understand their mental models and the specific frustrations they face. - You’re as excited to design a CLI tool or shape an SDK as you are to build a web dashboard. You’re ready to explore new frontiers like agentic workflows and AI-assisted design, not just standard web UI. - Design-engineering literacy: comfort near code, motion, or prototyping. - Writing, talks, or side projects that demonstrate your craft and point of view. If this role excites you but you don’t meet every single requirement, we’d still love to hear from you—your unique experience might be just what we need. BENEFITS - 4 weeks of paid vacation. - 14 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all parents to bond with a newly born, adopted, or fostered child. We will also work with you to create a supportive plan of return. - Long-term disability, life insurance, and 401K plans. - 100% employer-paid medical coverage and 99% employer-paid dental and vision coverage for you and a dependent. FSAs and HSAs are available as well. - Monthly lifestyle stipend for wellness, mental health and therapy, hobbies, etc. - Monthly cell phone and internet subsidy. - Commuter benefits for Renders in the Bay Area, and home office stipends for remote Renders. - Continuous learning benefits & related support. This position is generally not eligible for new visa sponsorship. At Render's discretion, the business may sponsor existing visa transfers. Applicants who require sponsorship must receive business authorization. Render is an equal-opportunity employer. We know that employing a team rich in diverse thoughts, experiences, and opinions allows our employees, product, and community to flourish. We make all employment decisions including hiring, evaluation, termination, promotional, and training opportunities, without regard to race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, physical handicap, mental disability, medical condition, disability, gender or identity or expression, pregnancy or pregnancy-related condition, marital status, height and/or weight. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. We encourage all who are interested to apply. We can't wait to hear from you! As Staff Brand Designer, you'll set the creative direction for how Render looks, sounds, and shows up. You'll take ideas from a blank page to a shipped campaign, build the visual system that holds it all together, and raise the craft bar for everyone who touches the brand. This is a senior IC role with real scope: you'll own work end to end, shape brand strategy alongside marketing leadership, and lead by example through the quality of what you make. What makes this work hard and interesting: developers are a famously skeptical audience. They can spot marketing gloss from a mile away, and they reward brands that are honest, specific, and a little bit delightful. Great brand work here has to earn attention from people who don't want to be sold to. That means ideas with real substance, design with genuine craft, and a voice that respects how engineers think. You'll make Render the booth developers go out of their way to visit. - Push graphic design craft to its highest level. Typography, layout, color, illustration, iconography, and art direction are your core tools. You'll produce work that other designers study, and you'll sweat the details that make it feel inevitable. - Build and steward the brand system. Evolve our visual identity, guidelines, templates, and asset libraries so that the brand scales with the company. You'll make it easy for others to do great on-brand work without you in the room. - Art direct and collaborate with outside partners. When the work calls for it, you'll brief and direct illustrators, photographers, motion studios, and agencies, keeping the output sharp and true to the brand. - Raise the bar across the team. As a Staff designer, you'll lead through your work and your feedback. You'll mentor other designers, contribute a strong point of view in weekly critiques, and help define what great brand work means at Render. - Partner across the company. Brand lives at the intersection of marketing, product, engineering, and leadership. You'll communicate clearly, align stakeholders around creative direction, and make the case for bold, considered work inside business conversations. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 10+ years of brand and graphic design experience, including time leading creative direction for a brand, campaign, or major launch. We care more about the impact and quality of your work than your title, but you've operated at a senior level and set the direction others follow. - World-class graphic design craft. jobs.title: Principal Brand Designer
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a Principal Brand Designer to define the brand design system that takes Ramp into new futures. You’ll turn our strategy into design, lead our most important brand projects, and help the team do its best work. This is a leadership individual contributor role. You can take any idea from zero to one. You understand the business fundamentals, the product value, the channels that perform best, and you know where brand design amplifies and improves the work. You understand each XFN’s accountability and outcomes, from product, marketing, GTM, growth and beyond. You can speak their language. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Set creative direction. Turn business goals and audience insights into clear ideas for the brand. - Lead company-defining projects. Take campaigns, launches, and other brand experiences from an open question to finished work. - Set the bar for quality and taste. You are the go-to expert for typography, imagery, layout, and brand design. You are the champion for this standard. - Build the brand system. Evolve our visual identity over time. We believe in coherency over consistency. We built our brand system to behave like jazz. - Connect brand and product. Work with product, marketing, and engineering so the company feels coherent wherever people experience it. - Raise the quality of the team’s work. You are a player-coach that can mentor others and develop a culture of collaboration, creativity, and trust. - Tell stories to drive alignment. Help partners understand the thinking, agree on a direction, and make practical choices about scope and timing. WHAT MAKES YOU STAND OUT - You’re already using AI tooling and agents to explore faster, iterate sooner, and develop ideas that you couldn’t before. - You have both agency and in-house experience. - You have side hobbies exploring design and creativity. We want to see side projects that show a desire for learning, a student-like mindset, and above all, enthusiasm for where the future is headed. - You’re humble, thoughtful, and self-aware. - Your portfolio reveals a story about how you’ve grown as a person, your interests, and curiosities. - You understand that execution is how good ideas win. WHAT YOU’LL BRING - A deep portfolio of brand identities, marketing campaigns, bringing brand into product experiences, and digital applications, with a clear explanation of your contribution. - Excellent design fundamentals and the ability to carry an idea through to finished work. - Experience leading complex projects independently and making good decisions when the brief is still taking shape. - The ability to negotiate, compromise, or understand trade-offs with executives and XFN partners. - The ability to connect creative choices to the audience, the product, and the business. - A record of helping other designers improve and working well with people across disciplines. jobs.title: Principal Product Designer - Diner Platform
jobs.descriptionText: This hybrid role requires working in the office two days per week. With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion. Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture. About the Job As a Principal Product Designer on the Diner Platform team, you will shape how millions of diners discover, book, and return to the restaurants they love, across our mobile apps and website. You will take on the most complex problems in acquisition, engagement, and retention, whether that means setting the vision for something new or stepping into a stalled project to find the way forward. You will work hands-on from early exploration through the build, and you will manage a small team of one to three designers while reporting to a Design Director. Your work will raise the quality and speed of design across the platform and help the designers around you grow. Responsibilities Set the vision for where the diner experience goes next, and bring teams along with it Step into messy problems, bring the right people together, and get something real to react to within days, then stay in the work through the build, shipping alongside engineers Manage a team of one to three designers, with regular feedback, coaching, and career growth Teach new ways of working, including AI-native workflows, and sharpen how we make design decisions Work with product, engineering, and data partners to balance diner needs, technical feasibility, and business goals, from discovery through booking Explain the work, and the thinking behind it, to senior leaders Minimum Qualifications 7+ years of product design experience, including leading design for complex consumer products A portfolio that shows design strategy, interaction design, and exceptional visual craft across iOS, Android, and responsive web Experience working with AI-native workflows Experience setting and driving design vision with partners in product, engineering, and research Strong written and verbal communication, including explaining and defending design decisions to senior audiences Experience managing designers **When applying, please include your online portfolio link and password in the application. We are reviewing portfolios thoroughly as part of the selection process and we appreciate the opportunity to learn more about you and your work. Thank you! Preferred Qualifications Experience scaling AI-native ways of working across a design team, not just in your own practice Fluency with front-end code, or experience prototyping in code A track record of using both insights and experimentation, like A/B testing, to guide design decisions Experience designing for marketplaces, discovery, or reservation and booking products A passion for food and dining Benefits and Perks 5 weeks paid vacation Private health & dental insurance Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year Focus on mental health and well-being: Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth Company-paid subscription to Headspace Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!) Paid parental leave Time off for your birthday Paid volunteer time Focus on your career growth: Development Dollars Leadership development Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings Travel Discounts Employee Resource Groups Income protection and life assurance Employee Assistance Program - including 24/7 GP & free legal advice Pension plan contributions Discounted gym membership Bike2Work Season ticket loan Social events & Thursday happy hours Free lunch 2 days per week The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility. Work Environment & Flexibility At OpenTable, we pride ourselves on fostering a global and dynamic work environment. As a team member with us, you will benefit from a schedule tailored to accommodate a global workforce operating across multiple time zones. While the majority of your responsibilities may align with conventional business hours, there will be instances where you are expected to manage communications - via calls, Slack messages, or emails - outside of regular working hours to effectively collaborate with international colleagues, respond to restaurant partners, and/or address urgent matters. OpenTable will always abide by and consider local laws and regulations. Inclusion We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. We know the best ideas come when we bring different voices to the table, so we're building a team as dynamic as the diners and restaurants we serve—and fostering a culture where everyone feels welcome to be themselves. If you need accommodations during the application or interview process, or on the job, we’re here to support you. Please reach out to your recruiter to request any accommodations. #LI-SK1 #LI-Hybrid

jobs.title: Staff / Principal Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: TL;DR - We’re seeking exceptional experienced product designers to help shape Lovable. You’ll lead projects end-to-end, collaborating closely with engineering. We expect a broad range of design skills, and exceptional taste. You’ll join a team at the forefront of AI, enabling anyone to create software. WHY LOVABLE? Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started. We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR - 10+ years experience working in high performing, fast-paced startup environments - A portfolio showcasing successful product work loved by users and produced in high-velocity teams - Talent for simplifying complicated user journeys into intuitive experiences - Strong prototyping abilities with emphasis on clear visual communication - Fluency with design systems and technical implementations - Outstanding command of visual design, UI patterns, and interaction principles - High aptitude for shipping and learning extraordinarily quickly - Bonus: You ship to production, perhaps with a little help from AI - Bonus: Experience designing AI products WHAT YOU’LL DO In one sentence: Design Lovable, making it the most Lovable piece of software ever. - Craft detailed user flows and high-fidelity mockups for new features - Own design projects from conception to delivery, collaborating with engineering or ideally implementing yourself with AI (we'll train you) - Be scrappy and hands on with any design assets needed - Establish scalable design processes that uphold quality standards - Champion quick wins and impactful improvements - Contribute to improving the design quality of Lovable's AI - Help set the bar for design quality and the culture for how design works at Lovable - Reinvent how teams work HOW WE HIRE 1. Fill in a short form then jump on an initial exploratory call. 2. We'll send you a quick take-home asking to present your best work over a loom video presentation. 3. Join us for a round of interviews to discuss your experience in more depth 4. Join us for trial work lasting 1-2 days remote or on-site. We'll see how you tick and you get to meet the team and explore whether joining Lovable feels right for you. Important Note: - Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join. - We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested please apply through our careers portal.

jobs.title: Staff Product Designer, Integrity
jobs.descriptionText: About the Team At DoorDash, design means making experiences for the people who order, the people who prepare, and the people who deliver. As a Designer at DoorDash, you want to build things that matter to real people. You're at your best when you can move from idea to shipped product quickly, bringing experiences to life that reach and influence users at massive scale. You'll care about whether the product you make solved a real problem for real people, or changed how someone experiences their day. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with Engineering and Product Management, dig into the data, and use LLM-powered tools alongside traditional design tools. If the LLM powered tools don’t exist yet, you build them. About the Role We’re looking for a Staff Product Designer to join our Integrity Design team and shape how DoorDash earns and protects trust across its three-sided marketplace. Integrity is a uniquely rich design space: every decision can affect a Customer’s confidence, a Dasher’s earnings and safety, a Merchant’s business, and the health of the marketplace itself. You’ll work across high-craft moments in the Consumer and Dasher apps and Merchant Portal, operational review tools, and AI-powered systems that detect risk, assemble evidence, and drive decisions. Your goal won’t simply be to block bad behavior. It will be to make those decisions precise, proportionate, and understandable—protecting good users, applying friction only where it’s needed, and making it painstakingly difficult for bad actors to exploit the platform. Your work will span fraud, trust, safety, and compliance, connecting the full service journey rather than optimizing a single screen or workflow in isolation. You’ll bring a strong human point of view to technically and operationally complex systems, shaping both how decisions are made and how consequential moments—verification, warnings, denials, or restrictions—are experienced. You will report to the head of Design for Customer Experience and Integrity, working alongside designers focused on support experiences and tooling, fraud, trust, safety, and compliance. This role is not 100% remote. We operate in a hybrid model with 1–2 days per week in our New York City office. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Define projects with a clear point of view on what to build, writing briefs that synthesize business and customer inputs into roadmap milestones; balance customer needs, business goals, and feasibility to shape what your team builds and why Bring clarity to ambiguous, cross-team problems and turn them into actionable work that ships; drive prioritization across your team and adjacent teams, making tradeoffs between design quality, speed, and impact so the highest-leverage work moves first Shape key projects from concept through execution — staying close enough to resolve issues during iteration, guiding design direction, and shipping work that drives measurable outcomes across multiple teams; produce high-fidelity designs and production-ready prototypes that set the craft standard for the team Design solutions spanning multiple workflows and contribute to shared tools — prompt libraries, component generators, workflow automations — that improve productivity across teams; mentor peers on responsible AI use and contribute reusable frameworks adopted beyond your own team Build trusted relationships across your team and adjacent product teams, influencing their roadmaps through evidence-based thinking and live prototypes that make your recommendations concrete; pursue consistent self-improvement and flex into raising team outcomes Multiply team capacity through mentorship, recruiting, and inclusive practices that raise the bar across your product group We’re excited about you because… You have a portfolio that shows projects that demonstrate craft excellence, systems thinking, and leadership through influence You reach for code editors and LLM-powered tools as naturally as design tools, prototyping in production and contributing meaningfully to the codebase You influence, design, and build solutions that work across teams and workflows You enjoy navigating unclear problems across multiple teams and create clarity through shipped artifacts, not slide decks You have a background in high-growth consumer tech or complex marketplace products Compensation The successful candidate's starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others. To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here . See below for paid time off details: For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year. For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week). The national base pay ranges for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more. Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. Designers at Databricks combine strong visual craft with systems thinking. They shape products used by some of the most advanced data teams in the world, and increasingly by the business users and AI agents working alongside them. We're hiring Product Designers to join our design team and own design for an area of the Databricks Platform. Teams span the platform, from data engineering and analytics to databases, apps, and AI agents. We match each designer to the area where their skills and interests will have the most impact. You'll design for both technical and business users of data, making powerful capabilities feel clear, controllable, and trustworthy for enterprise customers. The impact you will have Own your area end to end. Sharpen the problem, set the design direction, and carry the work from framing and interaction models through visual polish and shipped detail. Set the quality bar. Make the critical design decisions in your area, review work from designers, PM, engineering, and AI tools, and have the hands-on skill to improve it yourself. Advocate with evidence. Stay in regular contact with customers, choose research methods that fit the decision, and turn research into insights others can act on. Show the experience got better. Define what success looks like for the key tasks users need to get done, and show the improvement through usability testing, research, and how people actually use what shipped. Influence through the work. Move product and engineering decisions with prototypes, keep design reviews focused, and communicate clearly in writing and in person. Prototype to explore and align. Use interactive prototypes as a primary thinking tool to explore ambiguous problems, reduce risk, and align the team on a direction. Design directly in the codebase with coding agents. Use AI coding agents to ship well-scoped design changes alongside engineers, rather than handing off static mocks. Define reusable UX principles. Create interaction patterns and frameworks other teams reuse, and drive consistency through a strong, cross-platform design system. Raise the level of critique. Give and invite high-quality feedback, and help make clear decisions together with product and engineering. What we look for 5+ years of product design work experience. A bachelor's or master's degree in design, computer science, human-computer interaction, or a related field. A portfolio demonstrating your end-to-end design process, from inception to production. Demonstrated ability to lead large and complex design projects and balance the needs of diverse stakeholders. A systems thinker who has the vision to design the big picture, and the tactical ability to break it down so that engineering can succeed in building it incrementally. A deep understanding of business goals, customer needs, emerging AI capabilities, and the evolving data and technology landscape. Self-directed and comfortable in ambiguity. You help shape product direction when the path isn't defined. Beautiful visual and interaction work rooted in a data-driven, well-researched UX process. Nice to have Experience designing developer tools, data/analytics products, AI/ML products, or enterprise software. Experience designing products that bridge the gap between technical and business users. The strongest candidates have demonstrated experience using modern development and AI-assisted coding tools to prototype ideas, understand implementation tradeoffs, and collaborate deeply with engineering teams. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents.
