jobs.title: Head of Content Design
jobs.descriptionText: Asana is looking for a Head of Content Design to lead and grow our content design practice across the company. You'll manage a team of content designers working across our portfolio of products: Agentic Work Management, Service Management, Client Management, and Command. You'll set the standard for how Asana speaks to customers on every surface, from a settings page to a conversation with an AI Teammate. In this player-coach role, you'll lead the practice, develop senior practitioners, and take on some of the highest-stakes writing projects yourself while collaborating with the Asana Design leadership team to shape both what we make and how we make it. We design the future of teamwork. Asana has a bold, ambitious mission: help humanity thrive by enabling the world's teams to work together effortlessly. Our design team is at the heart of that mission. Asana Design is an inclusive and collaborative community. We're a diverse group of designers from different backgrounds (product, brand and content design, design operations, producers, motion design, film, copywriting). We are a team that loves combining research, data insights, and peer feedback into a human-centred design process to produce designs that are core to the power of our applications. We partner with people across Asana to create our product, shape our brand, and drive greater impact through design. We use design to solve challenges and create experiences that customers love. We also take the time to get weird and have fun along the way. We believe every designer should have the opportunity to grow and learn by utilizing their strengths and nurturing their interests. This role is based in our Vancouver office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. If you're interviewing for this role, your recruiter will share more about the in-office requirements. What you’ll achieve Lead, coach, and grow a team of content designers by setting clear expectations, developing their craft and careers, and building a team with a clear mission and measurable outcomes. Own the end-to-end quality of content across Asana's portfolio of products, including Agentic Work Management, Service Management, Client Management, and Command. Define and evolve Asana’s product voice, terminology, and content standards, building scalable systems—such as guidelines, patterns, design-system content, and tooling—that empower every product team. Establish Asana’s AI voice by defining the voice and tone for AI Teammates and agents, developing conversation design patterns, and distilling characteristics that make humans and agents feel like one team. Partner with Design, Product Management, Engineering, Research, and Product Marketing leaders to integrate content strategy into roadmap decisions and make content design a visible, measurable part of how Asana ships. Collaborate with Marketing and Brand Creative to ensure a cohesive voice and tone across the entire customer journey. Lead high-impact content design initiatives, including flagship launches, AI and conversational experiences, cross-product naming, and information architecture. Partner with Research and Data Science to validate content decisions through experiments and user studies, advocating for content improvements backed by evidence. Shape how the broader Asana Design organization operates as a member of its leadership team, including evolving design and content workflows alongside AI-assisted product development. About you Demonstrates curiosity about AI tools and emerging technologies, with a willingness to learn and leverage them to enhance productivity, collaboration, or decision-making 10+ years of experience designing content for digital products, including 4+ years managing content designers or UX writers and developing senior and lead-level practitioners. Proven track record of running a day-to-day content design practice—setting priorities across multiple teams, driving consistency, shipping products, and advocating for content design best practices cross-functionally. Demonstrated ability to build influence with Product, Engineering, and Marketing leaders so content design is embedded early in decision-making rather than treated as a final review step. Hands-on expertise in UX writing and content strategy for web and mobile products, covering microcopy, nomenclature, information architecture, accessibility, user education, and launch content. Experience designing content for conversational or AI-powered experiences, paired with a clear point of view on how products should communicate when systems generate language. Experience creating, governing, and scaling voice and tone guidelines and content systems—including AI content tooling—that cross-functional teams actively adopt. Proficiency in leveraging both quantitative and qualitative research to inform, make, and defend content decisions. Clear, persuasive written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting to executives and cross-functional leadership. We help our customers transport food, medicine, and other goods safely across the country, monitor deliveries for unsafe conditions, and help fleet managers improve the efficiency of their operations. Samsara’s Product Design team is responsible for crafting user-friendly features, workflows, and interfaces that our customers use every day to run their operations. jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Mapping
jobs.descriptionText: At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. For us, maps aren't just background graphics—they’re the core of the driver’s experience. While generic navigation apps focus on the everyday commute, Lyft Mapping is custom-built for the high-stakes, split-second realities of the rideshare experience. Drivers choose Lyft Maps because we solve the unique, complex challenges of living on the road: delivering glanceable turn guidance at speed, navigating tricky pick-up & drop-off dynamics, and providing real-time, AI-powered route assistance when every second counts. We build technology that empowers our drivers, transforms uncertainty into seamless flow, and sets the standard for real-time mobile navigation. We obsess over questions like: did your pickup spot feel safe and convenient? Did your driver feel confident following the route and arriving on the correct side of the road? Did you get stuck in unexpected traffic or road closures? You will tackle all of these challenges and more, with end to end ownership over the full ride experience, including driver navigation and rider pickup experiences. We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to advocate and maintain a user-obsessed culture within Lyft, and be happy and comfortable in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment. You'll partner with designers, researchers, marketers, and product managers to define and create top-notch experiences with safety as a core tenet for success. You’re experienced with every step of product development, from brainstorming broad ideas to ensure design quality through launch. Using your full range of interaction, visual, and product thinking skills, you will lead and own core Mapping experiences across our product teams. Responsibilities: Own core experiences end to end. Lead design for Mapping's most important user-facing surfaces, from problem definition through launch and iteration. Your primary areas, in order of focus: Core Navigation – turn-by-turn guidance, map zoom and motion details, and how drivers orient themselves with the road Real-time Feedback and Voice AI – how drivers report what's happening on the road, including emerging voice and AI-assisted experiences Map styling and 3D views – the visual language of the map itself, including 3D and map assets Map Tooling – internal tools that help Lyft's mapping and operations teams keep the map accurate Drive cross-organizational alignment. Proactively reach across organizational boundaries to partner with cross-functional leaders, synthesize competing feedback, and build consensus around complex design decisions. Work at the systems level. Build reusable design-system components, tooling, and map assets that improve the platform as well as individual features, so every surface built on the map gets better. Hold a high quality bar. Benchmark Lyft's map and navigation experiences against the leading map products, and use that bar to raise the quality of what we ship. Support accurate implementation. Partner closely with engineering and content design through build, edge cases, and launch, so what ships matches what was designed. Lead through ambiguity. Take complex, loosely defined problems, work with product and engineering leads to frame them, and drive alignment across teams with competing priorities. Raise the work (and work-ers) around you. Give critique that improves others' work, communicate complex design decisions clearly to broad audiences, including leadership, and help shape how the team works. Experience: 5+ years of product design experience, with a portfolio showing end-to-end ownership of complex, shipped mobile experiences Experience designing maps, navigation, or location-based products Strong craft in interaction and visual design , and the ability to prototype at high fidelity to explore and communicate ideas Strong advocate and experimental mindset with AI-native prototyping and tooling, whether code-based, AI-assisted, or both Upholds Design+ quality: Confidently interprets and applies UX Standards (Accessibility, Safety, Reliability, Usability, and Lyft Product Language) to work A proactive mindset driving cross-team collaboration, self-directed in ambiguity, and receptive to giving and receiving feedback across all levels A track record of systems-level work: design-system components, reusable patterns, tooling, or assets adopted beyond a single feature Close, effective partnership with product, engineering, data science and content design, including owning the details through implementation A rigorous quality bar, informed by deep familiarity with the best and most innovative map and navigation products Clear communication of complex, ambiguous work to broad groups and senior stakeholders Nice to have Motion design and 3D experience, especially for maps, animated components, and real-time interfaces Voice or conversational UI design experience Experience with driver, logistics, in-vehicle, or other high-stakes, glanceable interfaces Experience designing internal tools for operations or data teams Benefits: Extended health and dental coverage options, along with life insurance and disability benefits Mental health benefits Family building benefits Child care and pet benefits Access to a Lyft funded Health Care Savings Account RRSP plan to help save for your future In addition to provincial observed holidays, salaried team members are covered under Lyft's flexible paid time off policy. The policy allows team members to take off as much time as they need (with manager approval). Hourly team members get 15 days paid time off, with an additional day for each year of service Lyft is proud to support new parents with 18 weeks of paid time off, designed as a top-up plan to complement provincial programs. Biological, adoptive, and foster parents are all eligible. Subsidized commuter benefits Lyft is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other basis prohibited by law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Lyft highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture. This role will be in-office on a hybrid schedule — Team Members will be expected to work in the office 3 days per week on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. Lyft considers working in the office at least 3 days per week to be an essential function of this hybrid role. Your recruiter can share more information about the various in-office perks Lyft offers. Additionally, hybrid roles have the flexibility to work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year. #Hybrid The expected base pay range for this position in the Toronto area is CAD 136,000-170,000, not inclusive of potential equity offering, bonus or benefits. Salary ranges are dependent on a variety of factors, including qualifications, experience and geographic location. Your recruiter can share more information about the salary range specific to your working location and other factors during the hiring process. Lyft may use artificial intelligence to screen applicants, however, Lyft employees make the ultimate selection and hiring decisions. This job fills an existing vacancy.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Product Designer
jobs.descriptionText: The AI orchestration of your wildest imagination. n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact. Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve: - Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders - Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects - Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register http://app.n8n.cloud/register. We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us. We're looking for seasoned Product Designers who thrive in ambiguity and challenging problem spaces. n8n is a powerful, flexible technical tool, which means the problems you tackle as a designer are complex. Your design decisions must account for diverse user workflows, technical constraints, and how changes impact the entire platform. To thrive here, you will need to love talking to users, understanding technology, and reducing complexity and scope. You'll be embedded in a product squad alongside a product manager, engineering manager and around three to five engineers, owning the user experience for your area end to end. Our design team is small but growing, so you'll shape the craft bar and the culture, not inherit them. We're hiring designers across the following teams: - Enterprise (two roles: Governance & Observability, and Licence & Billing): You've worked on technical B2B platforms. You've designed for scale, governance and collaboration across teams, including permissions, environments, observability and failure modes, and you're comfortable making deeply complex systems feel coherent and simple. Governance & Observability gives admins visibility and the controls to enforce how n8n is used, from audit logging and execution diagnostics to admin settings. Licence & Billing covers licensing, subscriptions, usage-based billing and the cloud admin experience. - Knowledge: You have exceptional product sense and can connect disparate elements into a coherent whole. You'll take something complex, with many moving parts, and make it make sense. The team works on how agents and automations access company knowledge, and on core workflow-building surfaces such as data tables, sub-workflow execution and the canvas. Experience with data visualisation is welcome; deep technical expertise isn't required. - n8n Labs: As a Product Designer, you'll own discovery end to end: spotting the riskiest assumptions, running the research and turning findings into decisions without waiting on a brief. You move fast, cut scope without losing what matters, and you're hands-on enough to build and ship your own prototypes, including using AI tools to get there quicker. You've got product and business judgement, not just craft; you can spot an opportunity and make the case for it. Founder or co-founder experience is a helpful signal but not a requirement. Team assignment is confirmed at the offer stage and may be subject to change as the team structure evolves. 🎯 Regardless of the team, your main goal will be to lead end-to-end product design on complex workflows that elevate n8n's user experience, ship measurable outcomes, and raise the quality bar across our platform. To do so, here are your responsibilities: End-to-end product design - Lead the full design process for your team, from discovery to polished delivery, collaborating closely with PMs and engineers. - Consistently ship high-quality, visually cohesive designs that improve the overall UX at every release. - Work effectively on complex features and understand the underlying technology. - Take ownership of complex, multi-faceted problems and drive them to completion with initiative and autonomy. Research, feedback, and UX quality - Own the direction of research for your team: decide when it's needed, choose the right methodology, and take the initiative without waiting to be told. - Champion the user by talking to them regularly and running research that informs critical product and business decisions. - Master the feedback loop by gathering, synthesising and acting on input while giving actionable critique to elevate teammates' work. - Balance speed and quality in an MVP-driven environment, navigating ambiguity while maintaining a high bar. Systems thinking and platform coherence - Design in systems, integrating solutions into the broader n8n platform and safeguarding the product's big picture. - Account for edge cases, constraints and interaction details so users never end up in impossible states. - Collaborate across teams and designers to ensure consistency and quality across shared patterns and components. Strategy, impact, and innovation - Shape team strategy by influencing planning, prioritisation and scope with a strong design perspective tied to KPIs. - Explore and adopt AI and automation tools to push the boundaries of design practice and AI-powered workflows. Senior or Staff? We're open at multiple levels and we'll calibrate with you during the process, based on the scope you've operated at. At Senior, you own your squad's design end to end and ship work that raises the bar for your area. At Staff, you do that, and your influence reaches beyond your own squad: you shape patterns other designers build on, and you take on the problems that span teams. All levels are hands-on: this is not a step away from the craft. REQUIREMENTS Must-haves - 🎨 Product design excellence: You're proficient across product design, UX and UI, comfortable with qualitative research, and you deliver polished, detail-oriented work. - 🏗️ Complex product experience: You've designed complex, information-dense products, ideally technical B2B web products. Consumer-only or mobile-only portfolios are unlikely to be the right fit. - 🧠 Technical mindset: You collaborate effectively with engineers and understand how software is built, including common web technologies. You don't need to write code, but you do need genuine curiosity about what's happening underneath: APIs, webhooks, data structures and how workflows actually execute. - 🧭 Ownership & delivery: You've shipped end-to-end features in smaller teams or startups and can drive complex problems to measurable outcomes. - ⚡ Fast, focused execution: You operate at high speed in an MVP-driven environment, balancing quality and velocity amid ambiguity. - 📈 Outcome orientation: You use research and metrics to inform decisions and consistently deliver solutions that enable team KPIs. - 🤝 Feedback & collaboration: You're open and non-defensive in critique and provide actionable feedback that raises the team's bar. - 🧪 Curiosity for AI: You're enthusiastic about AI and innovation, actively exploring new tools and approaches to advance the craft. - 📅 Experience level: You have 5+ years in product design with demonstrable impact on shipped products. Nice-to-haves - 💻 Front-end fluency: You build with code or AI coding tools (HTML/CSS/JavaScript, vibe-coding) and collaborate effectively with engineers on the result. It isn't required, but it helps. - 🧩 AI & automation domain: You've designed AI or automation products; familiarity with n8n is a plus. - 🔁 Process improvement: You proactively refine team rituals and workflows to increase effectiveness. - 📚 Continuous growth: You invest in your craft and are motivated by creating tangible product and company impact. - 🔎 Discovery frameworks: You know methodologies like Continuous Discovery or Shape Up. - 📊 Data-informed design: You're comfortable with metrics, A/B testing or SQL to guide decisions. - 🚀 Entrepreneurial drive: You've built startups or side projects that show initiative and creative problem-solving. How we hire Our process has five stages: a conversation with our talent acquisition partner; a skills interview with a design manager, built around a short, low-fidelity design exercise; a whiteboard challenge with a design manager and a product designer; a portfolio presentation with a design manager and a product manager; and a final conversation with our VP of Product and Design. Why join us? At n8n, your work won't disappear into a slide deck. You'll lead high-impact design across core product surfaces, shaping AI-powered workflows, enterprise governance and billing, and how agents and automations work with company knowledge, from discovery to delivery. You'll join a fast-growing, Europe-based, remote-first company where autonomy, experimentation and craft matter, partnering closely with PMs and engineers to ship real outcomes to a passionate global community. Sound like a challenge you're excited to take on? Apply now and help us build the future of automation. n8n is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We can sponsor visas to Germany; for any other country, you need to have existing right to work. Our company language is English. You care about diversity and inclusion? We do too! Check out our Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging initiatives at n8n https://www.notion.so/Diversity-inclusion-and-belonging-n8n-c1bec2fff536422d868b1a438d990e35?pvs=21 (https://www.notion.so/n8n/Diversity-inclusion-and-belonging-n8n-c1bec2fff536422d868b1a438d990e35). jobs.title: Product Design Manager
jobs.descriptionText: The AI orchestration of your wildest imagination. n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact. Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve: - Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders - Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects - Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register http://app.n8n.cloud/register. We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us. We're looking for an experienced design manager to lead our Product Design team. This is a management role. Your job is to develop designers, raise the quality of the work, and make sure design has real influence on where the product goes. It is not a player-coach role, and it is not a step up for a strong IC looking for their first management position. We need someone who has already managed product designers and can do it well from day one. n8n is a powerful, flexible technical tool, which means the problems your team tackles are complex. Design decisions have to account for diverse user workflows, technical constraints, and how changes ripple across the whole platform. You'll need enough craft depth to recognise excellent work, challenge it constructively, and help designers get better. The team needs a manager whose design judgment they trust. You'll manage a team spanning product designers, design engineers and user researchers at a range of seniority levels, working across our product areas. You'll work alongside our other design manager. You'll report to our VP of Product until our Head of Design joins the team. That search is running now. More than 80% of workflows built on n8n involve AI agents, and we're widening from a developer audience to a broader set of builders. That shift is the central design problem here, and your team is at the centre of it. 🎯 Your main goal is to build a Product Design team that consistently produces excellent work and shapes how n8n's product evolves. Here's what that involves: LEAD AND DEVELOP THE TEAM - Run regular, high-quality 1:1s and coach designers, design engineers and researchers across different levels. - Own performance management: evidence-based reviews, honest feedback, and real support for anyone who isn't where they need to be. - Help people understand what's expected at their level and what growth looks like, evolving our progression framework for Product Design. - Hire excellent designers as the team grows, and broaden the range of backgrounds and perspectives on the team. RAISE THE DESIGN BAR - Set and hold a high standard across problem framing, user understanding, interaction design, information architecture and visual craft. - Facilitate design critiques and reviews that measurably improve the work, and help designers think beyond the feature in front of them. - Develop designers' judgment and autonomy rather than becoming the final approval layer for every decision. OWN THE WHOLE PRODUCT EXPERIENCE - Keep a holistic view across features and product areas, identifying inconsistencies, recurring UX problems, and opportunities for more coherent patterns. - Work with the team to address fragmentation systematically rather than feature by feature. MAKE DESIGN A REAL PARTNER - Partner closely with Product and Engineering leadership so design contributes early to problem definition and product direction, not late to execution. - Help designers influence product decisions through strong reasoning rather than positional authority. - Improve how the team works across critique, collaboration, decision-making and knowledge sharing, introducing structure where it helps the team scale and resisting process that slows things down. HOW MUCH OF THIS IS HANDS-ON? Worth being direct, because it's the question every good candidate asks. This is a management role: developing designers, raising the bar, and making design count in product decisions is the job, and that's where your time goes. You'll stay close to the craft in critiques, in reviews and in the detail of the work, and you'll occasionally pick up design work yourself. When that happens it sits outside the squads and varies with the period: an exploratory concept, a gap during someone's leave, a problem that needs a first pass. It is not a 50/50 split, and if what you want is to keep a squad's worth of delivery alongside managing the team, this isn't the role. REQUIREMENTS MUST-HAVES - 👥 Proven design management: You've managed product designers in a product-led technology company for 3+ years, with a team of five or more. This is not a first management role. - 🧭 Running a team well: You've run effective 1:1s, evidence-based performance reviews and difficult feedback conversations, including with people who weren't performing. You've built or improved a career progression framework for designers, and you're comfortable with the administrative side of managing a team rather than treating it as overhead. - 📈 Growing people: You coach and mentor, you run critique that changes the work, and you can point to specific designers who got measurably better or grew in scope while reporting to you. - 🎨 Design taste and judgment: Your own craft is strong enough that designers trust your read on quality, you can articulate what separates adequate design from excellent design, and you'll step into the work directly when the situation calls for it. - 🎯 Hiring: You've hired designers consistently well, you know where good design talent is and how to attract it, and you can tell the difference quickly. - 🤖 AI fluency: You use AI tools hands-on in your own work and in how your team designs, and you have an informed view on designing AI-enabled products. AI agents are the product here, so this one is not optional. NICE-TO-HAVES - 🛠️ Technical products: You've managed design teams in B2B SaaS, developer tools, workflow automation or similarly technical products. - 🧠 Technical mindset: You don't need to write code, but genuine curiosity about what's happening underneath (APIs, webhooks, data structures, how workflows actually execute) earns you credibility with engineers here. - 👩‍💻 Designing for developers: You've designed products for developers, technical operators or other sophisticated users. - 🔭 Systems view: You can step back from individual projects to spot patterns and UX problems across a broader product experience. - 🤝 Influence without authority: You bring Product and Engineering peers with you through reasoning rather than positional authority. - 📊 Scaling teams: You've grown a design team through a period of rapid company growth. - 🌍 Distributed teams: You've managed designers in remote-first or highly distributed organisations. - 🔓 Open source: You've worked on open-source or community-driven products. - 🌱 Inclusive hiring: You've meaningfully broadened the diversity of a design team through how you hire. OUR HIRING PROCESS We'll tell you the whole shape of it upfront, and there's very little homework. 1. Screening call with our recruiter. 45 minutes, no prep. 2. Leading designers with the hiring manager, 75 minutes. You'll present for 20 minutes on a team you built, grew or turned around. Reuse existing material; it shouldn't take more than two or three hours. We don't need case studies of your own design work. 3. Live critique and coaching, 60 minutes. We'll send you a real piece of n8n design work 24 hours ahead. You'll critique it, then have a coaching conversation with the designer who made it. No preparation beyond reading it and trying the product. 4. Conversation with our VP of Product, and a culture call with Jan, our CEO. 45 minutes each, same day where we can. 5. Meet two or three of the designers you'd be managing. Not scored; it's for you as much as for us. We'll also ask for two references, one of them a former direct report. A portfolio is welcome if you have one, though we know not every design manager keeps theirs current. WHY JOIN US? At n8n, your work won't disappear into a slide deck. You'll lead design for a product that hundreds of thousands of builders use to automate real work, sitting right where developer tools, AI agents and no-code interaction models meet. The design problems are genuinely hard and largely unsolved. You're inheriting an established team with strong designers, not building from zero, and there's real room to shape how the team coaches, critiques, grows and works with Product and Engineering, rather than inheriting a rigid design organisation. You'll stay close enough to the craft to influence quality directly, while your main job is making the designers around you better. You'll join a fast-growing, Europe remote-first company where autonomy, experimentation, and craft matter, at the point where n8n is scaling from a beloved open-source project into a major B2B platform. Design's contribution to product thinking is established here, and has a long way still to run. Sound like a challenge you're excited to take on? Apply now and help us build the future of automation. n8n is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We can sponsor visas to Germany; for any other country, you need to have existing right to work. Our company language is English. You care about diversity and inclusion? We do too! jobs.descriptionText: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Treasury brings business banking and payments together on Stripe. We help businesses receive, store, send, and spend their money in one place — with faster access to funds, global money movement, and cards for everyday spending. Instead of stitching together banks, payment processors, and financial tools, businesses can manage their money where they already run their payments. For design, this is an opportunity to rethink money management- an essential part of running a business. How might we make managing money feel effortless, help businesses operate across currencies and borders with confidence, and turn complex financial operations into intuitive, powerful experiences that give people more time to focus on building their businesses? We’re looking for a design leader to help shape those answers. Our ambition is to build products that are powerful, well-crafted, and beautiful—bringing the quality and care of the best consumer experiences to business financial tools. You’ll lead a team defining new experiences from the ground up, navigating substantial ambiguity and regulatory complexity without losing sight of what makes a product exceptional. What you’ll do Responsibilities Lead a design team focused on Treasury, shaping a compelling vision for a unified experience across business banking, payments, money movement, and spending Translate complex financial capabilities into intuitive experiences that help businesses access their funds faster, manage cash flow, and operate globally with confidence Guide zero-to-one work from early exploration through launch, helping the team turn open-ended problems into clear product direction and cohesive experiences Set a high bar for craft and beauty, coaching designers to deliver exceptional interaction design, visual design, and thoughtful details that build confidence and trust Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Legal, Compliance, Risk, and other stakeholders to find ambitious solutions within financial and regulatory constraints Build and develop a team of designers, growing their skills, judgment, and careers while fostering a high-performance, customer-obsessed team culture Inspire the team and align cross-functional leaders around a clear design vision, balancing long-term ambition with pragmatic progress and world-class excellence in what we ship Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. Experience leading design teams tackling complex products with technical or financial systems, including shaping zero-to-one products from understanding user needs and defining the problem to establishing a product direction and bringing it to market. Strong design judgment and a track record of helping teams deliver world-class, consumer-grade experiences. Ability to make sophisticated products feel simple, coach designers toward outstanding interaction and visual craft, and balance detail-oriented design with big-picture strategy, combining a deep understanding of users with business goals to drive meaningful outcomes Comfortable designing within regulatory constraints and partnering with legal, compliance, and risk teams. You can distinguish firm requirements from assumptions and find creative solutions without compromising user trust or regulatory obligations. Have demonstrated the ability to drive progress through substantial ambiguity. You bring structure to unclear problems, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and help teams move forward as requirements evolve. Excel at balancing detail-oriented design with big-picture strategy, combining a deep understanding of users with business goals to drive meaningful outcomes. Strong communication and collaboration skills, using storytelling and clear reasoning to align teams and influence senior stakeholders Preferred qualifications Experience designing financial products, particularly banking or bank-like experiences, money management, cards, or treasury tools. Experience delivering products across global markets with differing regulatory, operational, and user needs. Experience bringing fragmented tools and workflows together into a cohesive product experience with a consistently high standard of craft.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE Design at Ramp looks very different than it did a year ago: we’re building tools and agents, designing memory, shipping PRs, and rethinking the process every few months as new capabilities unlock. A few things have not changed, the role of design is to distill problems to their essence, obsess over craft and delight where it matters most, know customers deeply and advocate for them, lead with creativity and storytelling, and keep it fun, because a product built with joy always wins. We're looking for a Director of Product Design to lead a team of builders across some of our highest-priority bets. That means building a caring yet demanding structure, investing deeply in people — coaching, feedback, growth — so designers can do the best work of their careers and develop in this new age of Design. It’s never been a more interesting time to build. jobs.title: Principal Product Designer, Design Systems Lead
jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less. We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp. This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change. You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better. You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it. This role is for you if you’re excited by: - Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same. - Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality. - Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional. The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Lead and develop the design systems team. Set clear priorities, ownership, and goals. Give direct, timely feedback, hold people accountable, and help them do the best work of their careers. - Own the system’s vision and direction. Decide what to preserve, evolve, simplify, or replace based on what builders and customers need. Turn that direction into focused work the team can deliver. - Elevate Ramp’s visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path. - Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference experiences, composition rules, and guidance that produce better work without you in the room. - Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance, compose interfaces, and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use. - Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, work in code, and get into implementation details to test ideas, unblock the team, and understand where the system breaks down. - Define and measure quality. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks. Measure whether builders can ship better work faster, with less rework—not just whether they use the tools. - Improve the path from idea to shipped experience. Partner with engineering and AI teams on workflows that support fast exploration, useful iteration, and appropriate production safeguards. - Earn adoption. Work alongside product teams, listen closely, teach through examples, and turn recurring questions and exceptions into improvements to the system. - Keep the team moving forward. Experiment as models and tools evolve, share what you learn, and change direction when the evidence calls for it. WHAT YOU NEED - Experience leading and developing strong design or design engineering teams, with a track record of setting direction and delivering meaningful outcomes. - Exceptional visual and interaction design skills. Your work shows a clear point of view, attention to detail, and an ability to make complex experiences feel simple. - Deep systems thinking and experience building systems that other teams actually adopt. You can show how your work improved both their speed and the quality of what shipped. - Strong technical fluency. You can prototype and build in code, understand front-end architecture, and work through implementation tradeoffs with engineers—not just hand off specifications. - Active, hands-on use of AI in your design and building workflow. You understand where it helps, where it fails, and how to improve its output rather than accept it. - Experience turning design principles into practical guidance, reusable patterns, and quality checks that work at scale. - Strong product judgment and a habit of staying close to the people using what you build. jobs.descriptionText: Highbeam is building the future of business banking and cash management. Our platform combines AI agents, automated financial workflows, and integrated financial products that save brands time and money. Customers have generated billions in sales and include well-known brands such as Cuts https://www.cutsclothing.com/, Tushy https://hellotushy.com/, Rocco https://roccofridge.com, Sabah https://www.sabah.am/, Still Here https://www.stillhere.nyc/, Alice Mushrooms https://alicemushrooms.com/, Original Grain https://www.originalgrain.com/, birddogs https://www.birddogs.com/, and more. Our team includes alumni of Shopify, Square, Toast, Rippling, and McKinsey. We’ve raised $42M in equity from Acrew, FirstMark, Mayfield, and Two Sigma Ventures. [https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/7f0a2d9f-58d8-4b30-b1d9-7e652dfbd66d/962259dc-2fcd-40ed-8403-289c8a933cc7/image.png] [https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/7f0a2d9f-58d8-4b30-b1d9-7e652dfbd66d/a1d94b4e-50f8-4748-857e-9567893f3532/Ashby_Team_Img.png] ABOUT THIS ROLE We're hiring an extraordinary product designer: strong craft, strong product thinking, an exceptional eye. You'll be designer #2, working directly with our design lead (Rohail https://www.linkedin.com/in/rohail-khan1/) and CTO (Gautam https://www.linkedin.com/in/gautamgpt/), sharing ownership of the product's direction rather than executing specs handed down to you. What you'll work on - The financial platform, your primary focus: money movement, credit and capital, accounts, cards, and bill pay. Our customers are in these workflows every day, moving real money. - Luma, our AI financial analyst: scenario planning, cash flow intelligence, and spend insight. Few teams anywhere have shown what a trustworthy AI experience looks like when it handles someone's money. - The design system: the patterns and components the whole product is built from. You'll help set the quality standard and hold the product to it. Where design is headed here Design tooling and practice are changing faster than they have in a decade, and Highbeam is a product-led company where the design team controls its own trajectory: what we own grows as we show what design can do. Joining now means you set the foundations, and you help answer a question most of the industry is still guessing at: what does AI-native fintech design look like? WHO YOU ARE - 4+ years as a product designer, ideally in fintech, financial tools, or SMB products with a product-led growth motion. jobs.descriptionText: About the role We're looking for a Staff Product Designer to shape how DashPass delivers more value through affordability and new benefits. You'll join the Affordability pod within New Benefits, turning emerging customer needs into experiences that make everyday purchases more accessible and membership more valuable. This is a hands-on role with room to define the problem, set direction, and build. You'll work directly with product, engineering, research, analytics, and business partners to identify opportunities, test new concepts, and bring them to market. You'll connect a longer-term vision to the next experiment, staying close to the interaction, visual, and implementation details that make an experience feel simple and considered. We're building a team of designers who combine deep craft with the ability to bring ideas to life. You'll use AI throughout your workflow to explore possibilities, build working prototypes, and shorten the path from an idea to a shipped experience. Your judgment will shape both what we build and how the team builds it. You're excited about this opportunity because you will… Set direction in an emerging space. Turn customer insights, business goals, and incomplete inputs into a clear point of view, product briefs, and a sequence of experiments and launches. Influence what gets built. Build alignment with product and engineering leaders, shape priorities across the pod and adjacent teams, and resolve tradeoffs between customer value, feasibility, and business impact. Own the work from concept through launch. Move between problem framing, exploration, prototyping, and implementation, taking initiative to close gaps and keep the work moving. Deliver a high bar for craft. Create intuitive flows, precise visual design, and thoughtful interactions that make benefits and savings easy to understand and use, with accessibility and consistency built in. Build with AI. Use AI-assisted design and coding to make realistic prototypes, test ideas with customers, and contribute product improvements alongside engineers. Create reusable tools and workflows that help teammates move faster while preserving quality. Ship, learn, and improve. Partner with research and analytics to define success, evaluate experiments, and improve experiences based on customer understanding, benefit adoption, and membership engagement. Multiply the team's impact. Coach designers on craft and product thinking, share effective AI workflows, and strengthen shared patterns and hiring practices that raise the team's quality bar. We're excited about you because… Your body of shipped work demonstrates refined visual and interaction design, thoughtful systems thinking, and attention to the details of the final product. You've taken ambiguous opportunities from problem definition to launch, shaping what a team built and demonstrating what changed for customers and the business. You establish priorities and make progress with limited direction, identifying missing inputs, bringing the right partners together, and making decisions as new evidence emerges. You've influenced roadmaps and earned alignment across product, engineering, and business partners through clear reasoning, customer evidence, and tangible prototypes. AI is already part of how you work. You can show working prototypes, product changes, or reusable tools you've built with AI, explain your own contribution, and evaluate the quality of the output. You work directly with engineers on implementation, understand technical constraints, and use code to explore and refine an experience. You know when to explore broadly and when to narrow scope, balancing speed, craft, and customer value. You strengthen the work around you through critique, coaching, and shared practices. Experience with consumer subscriptions, marketplaces, pricing, savings, or benefits is a plus. jobs.descriptionText: ABOUT US Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar. Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes. 2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler. We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law. Joining Legora means three things. - We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions. - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback. - We grow together: as a team and with our customers. Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts. If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place. The role At Legora, we're building the category-defining AI product for legal work. Our users are lawyers. They read for a living and they notice every word. In an agentic product, words are most of the interface. Whether lawyers trust the product depends on getting that language right. As our first Content Designer, you will own the verbal layer of Legora. You will set the standards and encode them into our design system and the judgment tools our designers and agents draw on. This is a hands-on senior role. You will build the content design practice at Legora, working directly with product designers, PMs, engineers, legal engineers and our brand team. This position can be based in Stockholm, NYC, or London. What you will be doing - Define Legora's product voice and the principles behind it. - Design conversational and agentic experiences end to end: instructions, confirmations, progress updates, interruptions, handoffs, and how agents communicate results, sources and uncertainty. - Own naming and terminology across the product. Decide what things are called and keep the vocabulary consistent. - Write and shape in-product content with product designers on our highest-stakes surfaces. - Build content standards into how we work: design system guidelines, rules that automated PR checks can enforce, and guidance designers and agents can use on demand. - Make our agents into exceptional writers. Turn your judgment into instructions, examples and evals that coding and design agents follow, so on-voice copy is produced automatically and your time goes to the cases that need a human. - Partner with Brand and Product Marketing so the product sounds like the company that makes it. - Audit existing experiences and use customer feedback and product data to find where language is failing users. Who you are - Extensive experience as a content designer or UX writer on complex, high-stakes software products. - You have designed conversational or AI-driven experiences. - Exceptional writing and editing, combined with systems thinking: you see the patterns behind individual strings and build the frameworks that keep them consistent at scale. - Comfortable in ambiguity and in a domain where you are not the expert. You know how to extract the right vocabulary from lawyers and legal engineers and make it usable. - Fluent in how modern product teams build. You use AI tools in your own workflow. - Experience working in code, comfort with docs-as-code, and writing and owning agent skill files. - You make the case for content decisions with evidence and get product, engineering and leadership behind them. - Experience managing high demand work flow from cross-functional teams, ability to project manage and set expectations for your own deliverables Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. We welcome people of all backgrounds and don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Along the way, we’ve: - Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders - Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects - Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register http://app.n8n.cloud/register. We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us. n8n sits at one of the most interesting UX problems in software right now: more than 80% of workflows built on n8n today involve AI agents, and the platform is in the middle of a deliberate expansion from deeply technical developers toward a broader set of builders. That tension, keeping power users happy while dramatically lowering the floor, is the central design challenge. This is a foundational hire with a real mandate and direct exec partnership. WHAT YOU'LL DO OWN THE QUALITY BAR - Set a clear, consistent quality bar that the team can orient around and build toward, so great work becomes the natural output of how we design together. - Build review processes and critique rituals that give the team a shared language for quality and the confidence to make strong craft decisions together. - Evolve the design system and QA practices so the bar rises as the team grows. - Dig into one of the most genuinely interesting UX challenges in the space: n8n has historically had a steep learning curve for new users. Your job is to lower that floor without losing the power that experienced builders love. DRIVE DESIGN'S STRATEGIC INFLUENCE - Shape product strategy, not just respond to it. Bring design thinking into roadmap conversations and help surface user problems before they become someone else's brief. - Help lead n8n's expansion toward a broader, less technical audience, a deliberate and exciting strategic shift that design should be leading. - Build the kind of relationships with Product, Engineering, and leadership where design is a genuine thought partner at every stage. BUILD AND GROW THE TEAM - Lead a team of around 14 designers today: 2 Design Leads each working with ~6 ICs, plus Design Engineering and UX Research (with more hires ahead). - Shape the team structure, career framework, and progression paths so people know where they stand and where they're going. - Create a culture of high standards and honest feedback, where people feel supported to do their best work and have a clear sense of what great looks like. - Own hiring and headcount planning for the department, and help us grow without losing what makes the team good. BUILD RESEARCH INTO HOW WE MAKE DECISIONS - Establish a pragmatic, continuous research practice from the ground up. We're making our first dedicated UX research hires, so there's real room to shape this. - Make customer insight, product data, and community feedback a live input to product decisions, so teams are building from evidence at every step. - Connect research to the decisions that matter most: activation, adoption, retention, and helping new users find their way into n8n with confidence. HELP THE TEAM WORK IN NEW WAYS - Champion practical AI adoption inside the design org, from prototyping and research synthesis to design QA and workflow efficiency. - Help the team stay curious and current as the tools, patterns, and expectations around AI products continue to evolve fast. - Model the kind of working style you want to see: thoughtful, adaptive, and genuinely excited about what's changing. REQUIREMENTS MUST-HAVES - 🧭 Product design leadership: You have managed managers, coached senior designers, and built design teams that improve both craft and business outcomes, including making hard performance calls when needed. - 🧩 Complex product systems experience: You have led design across complex or developer-facing products where UX quality depends on deep product understanding. - 🎨 Craft authority: You are a quality bar, not just someone who appreciates quality. You can identify great work, explain why it's great, and hold the line on standards even when it's uncomfortable. - 📣 Strategic influence, not just strategic thinking: You have made design a co-equal in product conversations, not a downstream function. You know how to bring people with you, create debate, and drive decisions. - 🔀 Structured problem-solving under ambiguity: You find your way into unclear problems and create a plan. You don't just ask good questions, you answer them. You move forward when there's no map. - 🤖 AI-era product judgment: You understand the AI, automation, or adjacent tooling landscape and can turn emerging patterns into usable, trustworthy product experiences. - 🔍 Research literacy: You know how to build research into product development so insight becomes part of how teams make decisions, not a separate artifact. - 📊 Data-informed decision making: You use product analytics, research, and customer evidence to guide decisions instead of relying on taste or opinion alone. - 🧱 Org design and performance management: You can design team structures, define career paths, raise expectations, and handle difficult performance conversations with clarity. NICE-TO-HAVES - 🌱 Open-source or community product experience: You have worked on open-source, fair-code, community-led, or builder-driven products and understand what it means to design for a community that has strong opinions. - 💻 Design engineering credibility: You have enough front-end or design engineering fluency to partner deeply on design system adoption and implementation quality. - 🌍 Remote-first operating systems: You have built design rituals, critique, QA, and collaboration practices that work across distributed teams and time zones. - 🚀 Growth surface experience: You have worked on activation, onboarding, templates, time-to-value, or product-led growth surfaces. - ⬆️ Rising Design Manager profile: We are open to someone who has been an exceptional Design Manager and is ready for their first Head-level role, if the fundamentals are exceptional. n8n is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. jobs.title: Product Designer, Enterprise (Staff-level / L6)
jobs.descriptionText: Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US. As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations. Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow. Location: Europe remote or London hybrid THE ROLE: Synthesia is used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. The largest deployments now run thousands of creators across dozens of markets, languages, and compliance regimes. What decides whether those accounts expand or stall is not another avatar - it's whether admins, legal teams, and programme owners can actually stay in control. We're looking for a Staff (L6) Product Designer to own that layer end-to-end: workspace setup and governance, the content lifecycle, and the analytics and integrations that close the loop. This is the work that turns a proof of concept into a seven-figure renewal, and right now it is wide open. You'll operate as a senior IC: setting direction, influencing roadmap decisions (not just contributing), shaping bets with Product and Engineering leaders, and raising the bar on how we think about enterprise design problems. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING: - Own the Enterprise surface end-to-end, from problem framing to shipped outcomes and iteration - often dealing with ambiguity. You'll reach out to the right stakeholders, get the right eyes in the room, and make decisions independently. - Design complex governance and compliance systems that give admins, legal teams, and compliance officers genuine control and transparency. Examples include: - Permission models and role hierarchies that scale across thousands of creators without collapsing into chaos. - Audit log experiences that make compliance auditable - not just for the system, but for the humans who need to understand what happened. - Workspace setup and identity workflows that integrate with real enterprise infrastructure (SSO, SCIM, MCP). - License and billing models that admins can actually understand and manage at scale. - Analytics and reporting that tell admins whether their deployment is working as intended. - Work with technical constraints and possibilities. You'll develop fluency in APIs, widget architectures, developer hub patterns, and how backend systems shape what's actually achievable in the UX. You're not designing in isolation from engineering - you're designing in partnership with it. - Drive pragmatic iteration. You'll scope ruthlessly, build POCs to get signal early, and iterate based on what you learn from enterprise customers. - Set a design vision for our Enterprise surface and influence adjacent product areas to stay coherent. As things scale across SSO, compliance, analytics, and billing, you're keeping the mental model consistent. YOU SHOULD APPLY IF YOU BRING: - Significant experience designing complex, large-scale product surfaces - ideally admin dashboards, governance layers, analytics platforms, or other domains where system thinking matters. - Technical fluency. You understand APIs, integrations, how services communicate, how widgets and developer hubs work. You can read a technical architecture doc and understand the constraints it creates for design. You don't need to be an engineer, but you think like one. - Systems thinking: not just about interaction flows, but about enterprise systems. You understand how identity systems, compliance regimes, and scale constraints shape what's actually possible in the UX. You think in mental models and multi-step workflows, not single screens. - Comfort operating in ambiguity: you can turn unclear and fast-moving problem spaces into crisp direction, and you do not wait for perfect clarity. - Excellent communication in design reviews and cross-functional decision-making contexts. - Experience designing workflows where trust, transparency, and user control are central - helping users feel confident in AI-driven outputs rather than confused or excluded. - The ability to leverage feedback from users and customers to ensure the product continues to meet real needs - including enterprise users with high stakes around quality, compliance, and scale. AT SYNTHESIA WE EXPECT EVERYONE TO: - Put the Customer First - Own it & Go Direct - Be Fast & Experimental - Make the Journey Fun You can read more about this in this public Notion page: https://synthesia.notion.site/How-we-work-at-Synthesia-f794caa72f8446efb6be22b551ce0fa2 BENEFITS - A flexible, remote friendly role based out of Europe or one of our hubs in London, Copenhagen, Munich, or Zurich. - 25 days of annual leave + public holidays in the country where you are based. - A generous referral scheme. - Work from home set up. - At Synthesia, you can work from anywhere (within reason) in the world for up to 60 days per year! - A huge opportunity for career growth as you’ll help shape a market-defining product.
